production_fixes.defect: ProjectWriteHandler._submit_sql_hierarchy_operation freed its pending key only for ActiveBidLockedError and RuntimeError/ValueError. Any other exception raised by the queue submission (for example a LookupError or an OSError from the provider) propagated with the key still in _pending_sql_operations, so every later identical command (rename, move, trash, delete, duplicate, ...) silently returned False for the rest of the session. The SQL duplicate additionally disabled its action (busy flag) before the lookup/submission and never re-enabled it on such an exception. ConditionActionHandler already had the corresponding `except Exception: discard; raise` (scope7 fix); the project-tree handler lacked the same pending-key discipline.

findings: Production liveness defect: undeliverable queued-mutation cancellations retain their lifecycle-critical pending/journal metadata by design, but recovery cleared that metadata without re-checking mutation drains, so drain_database_mutations_async/drain_all_mutations_async callbacks (shutdown, reconnect, file operations) never completed. Fixed.

Comparison of queued-mutation cancellation with the repaired pending-edit rejection: both attempt every item, report the first dispatch failure only after draining and keep the session cleanup; edits additionally finish drafts (queued mutations own none), mutations retain recovery metadata per AGENTS.md. Retained operations are resolved only through query_operation and never replayed (tested for found=False and found=True). Residual, not changed: retained metadata for a stopped runtime is never cleared until the database reopens (PendingMutationRegistry.clear_database is unused), and runtime.cancelled_mutation_ids keeps cancelled ids until runtime death.

False positives: worker_releases_finished_edit_lease_before_overlapping_mutation (lock fake never conflicted, order unproven) and rapid_queued_mutations_wait_for_inflight_reconciliation (calls==[] trivially true) - strengthened and mutation-verified.

findings: Question: is the cancellation/recovery metadata retained for a STOPPED SQL runtime a defect? Answer: NO. Neither stale-metadata effects on a later runtime nor unbounded growth reproduce, so per the decision rule the unused PendingMutationRegistry.clear_database was deleted and the retained-and-bounded behaviour was pinned by a test.

Only source of retained metadata: _reject_pending_mutations (run from _reset_session in the worker's finally) dequeues every queued mutation and dispatches CANCELLED_BEFORE_START; if the UI-bridge dispatch raises, the failure is reported after the batch drains and that operation's PendingMutation (QUEUED, old runtime_generation) plus its journal record stay. The UNCERTAIN/RECOVERING cases (commit status unknown, projection failed) are likewise retained by design for durable-outcome recovery. Readers of the retained metadata: _recover_journaled_operations (journal.list_all filtered by database_id; queries the durable outcome and never executes the operation), _project_session_start (finishes entries whose durable outcome was found and have no live callback, or completes the callback), _complete_mutation_drain_if_ready (lifecycle-critical QUEUED/EXECUTING/PROJECTING entries block drains), _publish_pending_mutation_state (pending_count) and cancel_queued_mutation.

(a) Stale effects on a later runtime: not reproduced. A restarted runtime (new generation + new session) cannot cancel the stopped runtime's operation (cancel_queued_mutation checks pending.runtime_generation == runtime.generation and state QUEUED), recovery queries only the retained operation ids, never calls the operation callable (writes stay []), clears registry/journal/_uncertain_callbacks, and a new mutation then queues and executes once; the drain for the database completes immediately after recovery. Registry metadata is not consulted for resource blocking at all (only drain and pending_count), and begin() duplicate-ID rejection only affects the same operation id until recovery resolves it (a runtime cannot be established, hence cannot accept queue_request, before _recover_journaled_operations ran).

(b) Unbounded growth: not reproduced. Measured with a real-thread coordinator (start_database/_stop_database, fake _RecoverableProjectionStore, journal fake, dispatcher failing every _complete_mutation_request on stop): after N=50 and N=200 stop/start cycles each stop left exactly 1 registry entry and 1 journal record (max (registry, journal, uncertain callbacks) = (1, 1, 0) at every cycle, dropped cancellations 50/200, writes executed 0). Each new runtime resolves the previous one's entry before it can become established, so the steady state is at most the last stopped runtime's undelivered operations. The new deterministic test asserts the same for 50 cycles. Experiment script: scratchpad/exp_cancel_metadata.py.

Residual, intentional behaviour (not changed): for a database that never gets a new runtime, the retained QUEUED lifecycle-critical entry stays in memory and would keep drain_database_mutations_async for that database pending until a runtime starts a session or the process exits (the durable journal record then drives recovery on the next process start with an empty registry, which just removes the record). This is the behaviour already pinned by test_recovery_releases_lifecycle_drain_blocked_by_retained_cancellation and is the AGENTS.md rule 'Retain undelivered operations recovery metadata'. Clearing it on stop would drop that blocking and the in-memory recovery state, so wiring clear_database into stop was rejected. It requires the UI bridge itself to fail during stop, so it is a narrow corner; flagging it for the user only as a design note.

Vulture-style audit of PendingMutationRegistry: begin, transition, finish, get and for_database are all used by production (sql_collaboration_coordinator.py); clear_database was the only unused public member (referenced only by its own test) and was deleted. No docs or tools reference it (only stale Nuitka build artefacts under dist_visualizer mention the module name).

Production change (dead code removal, not a defect fix): ost_visualizer/application/services/pending_mutation_registry.py loses clear_database and gains a short class docstring recording that entries are released only per operation by finish() and that undelivered-cancellation metadata is intentionally kept for the next runtime to resolve.

findings: TransactionMonitor invokes both the commit callback and the status callback on its own worker thread ('TransactionMonitor'); it does not marshal. This is by design: the callers marshal (VisualizationService._on_monitored_file_changed goes through callback_bridge.dispatch; service_builder wires set_ost_status_callback to OstSignaler.emit_status, a Qt signal; QtMessageNotifier.post_message emits a Qt signal). The monitor itself never touches EventBus. Pinned in test_worker_dispatches_on_its_own_thread_and_stop_joins_it.

Not reproduced / design note: any unexpected wait result (e.g. WAIT_FAILED=-1 from WinEvent.wait on a closed handle or failed DuplicateHandle) only logs a warning and leaves the event in place, so _monitor_loop would spin without waiting and log every iteration. WinEvent.wait only returns -1 immediately when the handle is already closed, which this class never does while the loop runs, so no real trigger was found; no production change. The test asserts the warning and no dispatch only, not retention of the event.

Not reproduced / design note: WAIT_ABANDONED and processing-exception resets set _status_online False silently (no ost status callback), so the UI could keep showing 'active' until the next status transition if the reconnect finds OST offline. Contract unclear; not changed.
Design note: the debounce callback runs while holding _debounce_lock, so a callback re-entering start/stop on the worker thread would deadlock/raise; current consumers do not.

POSIX gates in tests/sql_server/python/ostv_sql_admin: the requirement is real for the five tests that exercise require_private_file/require_private_directory/_require_private_root/_read_public_wireguard_key (0600/0700 modes and st_uid == 0). findings: Reproduced against the real stack: delete Hot Link, delete its Named View separately (no cascade confirm since the link is already gone), undo (Named View restored under new persisted UID when other Named Views have higher UIDs, e.g. 5 -> 10), undo again: the Hot Link history entry still carries the old BidPageViewUID, the MDB writer (require_existing_bid_scoped_uid_matches on BidNamedViews) refuses the dangling target, the composite paste fails (incomplete UID map), the undo returns REJECTED. No persisted/model corruption and no orphan, but the Hot Link entry stays on top of the undo stack READY so every later Undo silently does nothing (no warning dialog) and older history is unreachable; the newer Named View deletion remains redoable.

Reachable in the real UI: Hot Link and Named View deletes are separate batches when the link is deleted first (annotation-only fast path on_elements_deleted, also detached window DeleteAnnotationsCommand and SQL _push_sql_delete_history share the same pattern of storing a spec with the old target uid and no Named View lifetime dependency).

Production gap (design level, NOT changed): Hot Link delete history retains no Named View lifetime dependency (unlike Takeoff external parents via _history_parent_targets), so a Named View restored under a new UID is not followed. Same class would apply to Hot Link paste/placement history redo. A proper fix needs a decision: (A) Hot Link follows the restored Named View via a retained dependency target in annotation_targets plus remap at restore in each delete/paste history path (handler fast path, _push_mdb_delete_history, _push_sql_delete_history, detached window); (B) keep refusal but surface a message and let the user discard the stuck entry; (C) restore with a null target. AGENTS.md does not specify, so no behaviour change was made. SQL path not exercised (no SQL server stand-in): it also adds a resource dependency on the old Named View UID and would be expected to refuse.

findings: No production defect was found in the 25 modules; every mutation survivor was an equivalent mutant or is covered by another module, listed in the per-test notes.

Live-SQL modules (client_development, collaboration, environment, lifecycle) were NOT executed: they need OSTV_SQL_* opt-ins, a localhost SQL Server with a server marker, and (client/lifecycle) the owned development environment or a disposable machine. All gates are legitimate, were confirmed to skip, and the edited files were compiled with py_compile; the edits are small and were reviewed line by line, but are unproven against a real server.

Safety gaps fixed in the live tests: server-level logins were created before the disposable server marker was verified (collaboration x2, environment role test); the persistent client development database had no marker check before writes; password comparisons used assertEqual/assertNotEqual/assertNotIn which echo secrets on failure (client_development, lifecycle, collaboration); the first of two test logins leaked if the second creation failed.

Four modules defaulted to the native Qt platform when run alone (test_detached_restore, test_creation_identity, test_tree_indentation; test_layers_indicator/test_windows_startup intentionally use the native windows platform in subprocesses and are skipped off Windows); the first three now default QT_QPA_PLATFORM to offscreen so they never open windows on the real desktop or depend on real screens.

test_layers_indicator and test_windows_startup need the native Windows platform and desktop session; they depend on the installed Windows Qt style rendering (not on fonts or DPI). Mutants in the child process were checked by running the same check function in-process through scratch drivers.

Mock policy: the reader stub in test_global_condition_scope/test_global_bid_family_scope remains a plain Mock() because spec'ing it as SqlProjectReader flips an isinstance branch in SqlRemoteChangeReader.hydrate_connection; all other bare Mocks in the SQL modules were replaced with create_autospec or explicit fakes. The visibility coordinator tests keep SimpleNamespace explicit fakes around real sidebar, coordinator handlers and DeferredPersistenceManager.

Mutants not killed and judged equivalent or covered elsewhere: active-change Bid filter in RemoteChangeReconciliationService.apply (both fixture Bids carry the same families); LoadBidUseCase token-currency gate (navigation modules); explicit showMaximized/showFullScreen in _show_initial_window (restoreGeometry already restores state); themed_icon cache clear (cache keyed by colour); Windows 11 style vs Fusion brush policy; _applying re-entrancy guard of the toolbar controller; header controller no-op write skip and persisted-width intersection; sort-indicator re-hide by setSortingEnabled; SqlConnectionDialog creator-mode title (presentation tests); DeferredPersistenceManager revision cleanup and restore expansion (deferred manager unit tests).

graphics_items.py: sweep of 106 mutants killed 92 with 14 equivalent survivors (null-image guard operands because Qt makes every zero-dimension QImage 0x0; hypot argument swaps/sign flips; QPointF(0,0) arg swap). The set_clip_rect update() removal survived the original tests and is now killed by ClippedTextRepaintRequestTests.

handle_style.py: sweep of 25 mutants killed 16; the 9 survivors are all in the unused-background fallback `background_color if background_color is not None else QColor(255, 255, 255)` because handle_colors_for_background ignores its background argument (documented by the credited tests that pass None, dark and light backgrounds). Equivalent.

No test in these files used font-dependent geometry; paint tests sample block-centre colours with a tolerance and use alpha-0 pixels as the negative control. test_clipped_text_set_clip_rect_notifies_the_scene_of_old_and_new_bounds depends on a 30 ms qWait for the scene's deferred changed signal; it passed in every run and in the 1608-test plan_view sweep.

limitations: Exact 22.5/67.5/112.5/157.5 degree cursor-band boundary operators are not pinned: the boundaries are float-angle measure-zero and any exact-hit vector would depend on platform atan2 rounding.

findings: Full AST mutation matrix of drag_handler.py (2134 mutants, 259 tests, no fail-fast): 2041 killed, 93 survived. The only killable survivors (corner_count > 0 boundaries at L301 and L339) are now killed by the two new SingleCornerHandleSweepTests; the remaining 91 are equivalent.

Equivalent survivors, by reason: symmetric argument swaps (setPos(0.0,0.0), QPointF(0,0), math.hypot, min/max, abs differences, zip inside the symmetric math.isclose, cos(a-b) vs cos(b-a) at L553); slices/ranges that Qt or even-length vertex lists make identical (area_pts[1:] -> [0:] only adds a duplicate lineTo that QPainterPath drops; range(2,len-1,2) -> range(2,len,2) on even-length transformed lists); redundant guards (len(tx)<2 after 'not tx'; is_curved_linear re-checked as len(new_pos)>=6 at L469/L569; the final elif len(tx)>=2 and n_h>=1 after earlier returns; 'orig and' before len(orig)>=start+2; is_body_move index>=0 after the -1 case; handle_idx<2 vs <=2/<3 at L335/L343 because the curve-control branch consumes handle 2 first); positions with <6 values give empty paths in position_polygon_path and are rejected by path_is_inside / skipped by path_intersects_any (L1030, L1047-1048, L1077-1078; L845/L881 degenerate children subtract no area and closeSubpath removal does not change a boolean result); _attachment_footprint_path already returns an empty path for non-attachments (L921 operand 4); condition types are mutually exclusive so the dropped continue at L1001/L1026 reaches the same result; early-return drops at L804/L813 fall through type checks that cannot match; _drag_item_orig_positions is always a dict (L733); 'condition.is_area and takeoff.is_hole' (L964) and the L970 early return only restructure equivalent control flow; native polygon_is_valid already rejects fewer than 3 points (L92).

No production defect found in drag_handler.py; the one oddity noted (edge handle with corner_count=1 applies the delta twice because ci0 == ci1) is an unreachable degenerate input, not pinned by any test and not changed.
evidence.validation: ./venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest tests.presentation.components.plan_view.components.test_drag_handler -q -> Ran 261 tests OK (259 before this batch plus 2). ./venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests/presentation/components/plan_view -t . -q -> Ran 1614 tests OK. mutrun.py on both new tests: corner_count > 0 -> > 1 (L301) KILLED, elif corner_count > 0 -> > 1 (L339) KILLED. Automatic mutation matrix (dh_matrix.py over automut mutants, 2134 mutants, computed before the two additions) analysed for survivors. eolcheck.py check: eol ok, no new files.
limitations: The kill matrix was computed before the two SingleCorner tests were added (they only add kills). Equivalence of the 91 survivors was established by reading production and helper code (geometry_utils guards, Qt path de-duplication probed directly), not by an automated equivalence prover.
The unreachable corner_count=1 doubled-delta quirk is deliberately not asserted.

findings: Sweep of input_handler.py lines 1-1656 (ids 0-1861 of 3786 AST mutants, tools: SCRATCH/automut.py gen + sv1/fastmut.py in-process swap, 60 random KILLED verdicts re-verified out of process): 1862 mutants, 7 header-only mutants (defaults) killed out of process, 1801 killed in the sweep, 54 survivors at first pass; 10 of those killed by the new/strengthened tests above; the remainder are equivalent: L141/L142 [:2] slices on 2-value lists, L145 [4:5] vs [4:6] (only differs for >5-value text positions, not a supported shape), L213 early return in _restore_drag_preview_positions (nothing to restore anyway), L264 uid operand (pop(None) is a no-op), L373 delta_y >= 0 (zero delta returns earlier), L499 return (a following check swallows non-right buttons), L518/L628 _editing_enabled and button operands (ROTATE modes are swallowed by _editing_cursor_mode_allowed() first, and the label guard needs a left button anyway), L606/L687/L1143 swapped identical or symmetric arguments, L608 event.accept() in the ZOOM press (overwritten by the trailing super().mousePressEvent which ignores the event), L654 re-assignment of the uid already stored at L644, L715 (None in selected is False), L758 break (idempotent flag), L798/L889/L932/L933 redundant re-clears of state cleared at L741 or L738, L862 can_resize operands (every inner annotation type is resizable), L888/L916 operand variants (len==1 handled earlier; plan uid and original position are always set together), L935 return before an identical accept, L1013 +180 vs -180 (equal modulo 360), L1102 range end on an even-length list, L1116/L1230 sign-symmetric deltas (abs / manhattanLength / isNull), L1175/L1404 text-move handle operand (interactive text with handle >= 0 takes the resize branch), L1202/L1448/L1462 argument swap of the symmetric _positions_meaningfully_different, L1369 resize_release uid/original operands (already required by the enclosing condition).

ZOOM-mode left press (input_handler.py L601-608) calls event.accept() but then falls into the trailing 'else: super().mousePressEvent(event)' (L961-962) which leaves the event unaccepted; observable but harmless, not changed and not asserted.

A middle press in ZOOM persistent mode with no remembered pre-zoom mode stores ZOOM itself as the pre-zoom mode (test_middle_press_in_zoom_without_a_remembered_mode_does_not_restore pins this); not reproduced as a defect because reaching it needs the persistent mode to be set to ZOOM by another path, so left unchanged.

findings: Second half of input_handler.py (_should_defer_text_annotation_press_side_effects .. changeEvent, lines 1657-3277): in-process AST sweep of 1924 mutants. Before this batch 298 (+3 timeouts) survived the module; after the 92 new tests 76 survive and every one is equivalent or dead code (see the next findings); the three timeouts (ids 2085/2087/2090, the loop guard of _area_child_parent_map) are infinite loops killed by the existing cycle-termination test through a hang and were not re-run.

mouseReleaseEvent (lines 1243-1656, shared with the first-half agent): with the module's tests at the time, 5 of 464 mutants survived. One (text_move without the handle == -1 operand) is killed by the new InputHandlerReleaseTextMoveSweepTests test; four are equivalent: _positions_meaningfully_different is symmetric (two argument-swap mutants) and the `uid is not None` / `_drag_orig_position` operands of resize_release are subsumed by the outer `self._drag_plan_item_uid and self._drag_orig_position` guard.

Equivalent or dead survivors in the second half. (1) preserve_zero_axes of _compute_group_translation_positions has no observable effect: a zero axis is translated by snap_ost(0) = 0, so copying the original value changes nothing; its default, the `if preserve_zero_axes` test and the True argument in the keyboard move cannot be pinned (the start-index mutants inside that block ARE killed by the new parity test). (2) Symmetric or absolute-value rewrites: abs(nx2 - nx1), abs(ny2 - ny1), abs(vp.x - handle.x), math.hypot argument order, min/max argument order in _takeoff_transform_center, QPointF(0, 0) swaps, _positions_meaningfully_different argument order. (3) Redundant guards: `ann and ann.is_interactive` (a non-interactive annotation and a takeoff never share a uid), the len(pos) >= 5/4/3 text guards (stored rotation and bbox exist only for longer positions), ink `len - start < 2` (always even), the null checks that cannot fail with the real expansion, `if not uid: return` in _apply_slope_rotation (followed by .get(None)), the early `return` after the slope branch of _restore_rotation_handles_if_needed, the has_changes / has_rotations / rotated_uids bookkeeping and the default arguments of the transform helpers, the left/top/right/bottom None checks (all four are None together), the `return None` guards in _polygon_control_point_position that repeat what _polygon_control_point_model_position and polygon_is_valid already guarantee (point_count < 3, odd length, point_count <= 3 on vertex removal, len(area_pts) < 3), `action is not None` operands in the contextMenuEvent dispatch chains, and the last `return None, None` of _add_polygon_control_point_context_action (unreachable: unknown kinds return None earlier).

Fixtures that already held the expected value in the pre-existing tests (fixed by the new tests; nothing was weakened): rotation about the first point used a (0, 0) origin so x/y indices were interchangeable; the rotate-handle hit test used a handle at the origin; keyboard move and multi-drag preview used the symmetric delta (10, 10) so axis swaps and own-vs-fallback outline deltas were indistinguishable; area rotation asserted its children but not the area's own polygon; hole validation stubs ignored their arguments.

Runner note: mutants were run with a purpose-built in-process runner (scratchpad ihs2/inproc.py) that patches the compiled mutant methods onto InputHandlerMixin and onto test classes that copy mixin functions by assignment (_OwnedPlanMenuHarness); a no-op mutant SURVIVED as baseline.

limitations: The in-process runner only patches methods of InputHandlerMixin (and copies of them in test classes); the 3 infinite-loop mutants of _area_child_parent_map were not re-run.

mouseReleaseEvent was swept here only to confirm coverage for the six owned release classes; the first-half agent owns its remaining survivors.

findings: User decision A implemented: a deleted, pasted or placed Hot Link follows its Named View only when that view was reactivated through the accepted restore map of the history entry that deleted it (lifetime target mechanism modelled on Takeoff external parents). Otherwise the restore is refused cleanly with an explicit warning dialog (no new UI) and nothing is written.

Placement redo (_insert_annotations_with_undo) and MDB paste redo reproduced the same gap and were fixed with the same helper; SQL delete/paste history and the detached window paths (delete, SQL delete/insert history, hotlink placement, annotation paste) share it and are covered against fakes.

After a refused restore the entry stays on top of the undo stack (existing semantics for a failed transition); it is now announced by a warning on every attempt instead of being silent. Discarding such an entry was not added (new behaviour/UI).

Known limit (same as Takeoff lifetimes): a Named View deleted outside any history/lifetime event whose uid is reused on the same Page by an unrelated view while the retained target still looks available cannot be told apart; cross-window deletions are covered through ANNOTATION_LIFETIMES_DELETED invalidation.

Hazard: a refusal opens a modal QMessageBox, so any test that can trigger it must patch show_warning (a mutant that broke dependency retention hung the offscreen run until the tests patched it). The chaos harness and the new classes patch it.

findings: First-half mutation sweep of ost_visualizer/presentation/components/plan_view/view.py (lines 1-3186, up to and including get_annotation; the second half starts at _restore_annotation_positions) with an AST mutation generator: 3051 mutants (operators, constants, early returns, removed calls/assignments, argument swaps). Against the pre-existing module only 1821 were killed (1220 survived/hung). After the 328 new tests all 3051 are accounted for: 2959 killed (including 4 non-terminating-loop and several interpreter-crash outcomes) and 92 equivalent with a written reason each (SCRATCH\sv4\marks.json; categories: swapped equal arguments, symmetric helpers, Qt defaults, redundant guards, int() truncation hiding a default, offscreen having a single font family). Final verification: the whole sweep was re-run against the integrated test_view.py module, and 160 randomly sampled kills were re-confirmed in fresh processes (160/160 killed).

Uncovered areas the previous 288-test module left to other test files (all now pinned in test_view.py): TakeoffPlanView.__init__ state/wiring and the class-level constants; the condition text toolbar construction; the loading/missing-file overlay bars and tokens; condition/dimension/named-view label hit testing and toolbar targeting; inline text and named-view editing (begin, drafts, teardown, document hooks, focus, rename validation, shortcuts); text style persistence (takeoff fonts, annotation fonts, colours, widths); condition label placement; layer and page-image visibility; scene rect/centre handling; view-state capture/publish, the load cycle and the view contract; PDF text extraction mapping/hit testing/selection; backout context validity.

The 97 uncredited overlay-move tests (Lifecycle 19, Visual 24, OverlayPreview 21, Handle 21, Sweep 12) were mutation-checked with 734 AST mutants of view.py lines 3959-4608 (the overlay-move methods): 657 killed. The 77 non-killed mutants are not in methods those classes target (_commit_overlay_move and has_active_remote_projection_blocker belong to other classes' tests) or are equivalent (QPixmap/setOffset/hypot argument swaps, symmetric OUTLINE_OFFSETS, the unused overlay tint colour values, isValid operand redundancies). Per-test attribution (non-fail-fast run) shows every one of the 97 tests fails for at least one mutant (minimum 1: test_overlay_rect_tuple_normalises_numbers_and_rejects_malformed_values).

Four of the 97 tests were strengthened: test_loaded_overlay_preview_without_a_preview_rect_uses_the_current_page (only asserted that an item exists; now pins the transform against an explicit equal rect and a moved rect, killed mutant: swapping the preview_rect/current_page branches), test_loaded_overlay_preview_becomes_a_scene_item_with_the_preview_transform (the title promised a transform that was never asserted; killed mutant: passing scale 1.0 to _create_overlay_graphics_item), test_overlay_render_scale_depends_on_the_overlay_file_type and test_overlay_preview_request_renders_the_page_copy_with_the_new_rect (added literal 3.0/1.0/rotation 0 beside the self-referential helper comparisons; killed mutants: always-PDF baseline scale, hard-coded rotation).

Named weak spots checked first. test_cold_composite_first_move_keeps_one_overlay_through_stale_frame already kills mutants that drop the hidden-normals sync (page_loader._sync_overlay_move_hidden_normal_visuals) and the stale-frame suppression guard, but a mutant that disabled the tile-coverage suppression (page_loader._update_tile_coverage: if self._overlay_move_suppresses_normal_tiles()) survived it; it now also asserts that no composite frame request is issued while the overlay is being moved (mutant killed). test_highlight_remains_observable_across_page_image_modes_and_layer_state kills mutants that raise the move-preview base or overlay z above the highlight (pixel assertions) and was left unchanged.

Test-order dependence found and fixed: TakeoffPlanViewStateAndFlushTests.test_ost_positions_convert_to_scene_points_through_the_page_scale (owned by the other sweep agent) mutated the process-wide FakeTakeoffRenderer.coordinate_system (view_scale 2.0, scale_ratio 4.0) without restoring it, so test_text_annotation_font_size_increase_preserves_box_geometry and test_text_annotation_font_size_change_keeps_clip_rect_on_stored_box failed in reverse/shuffled order. I added two addCleanup calls restoring both attributes in that test (additive edit); the module now passes in default, reverse and one shuffled order (1024 tests each). My own geometry tests that depend on the coordinate system install a private FakeCoordinateSystem instead of the shared one.

Runner caveat discovered and handled: the first in-process mutation runs produced false kills in batches that followed that shared-state pollution (workers reported POISONED). Those verdicts were discarded: the full 3051-mutant sweep was re-run on the integrated module after the fix and its 29 non-killed verdicts (beyond the documented equivalents) were each addressed by a new/strengthened assertion or a written equivalence.
No production defect was found in the first half of view.py; no production file was changed.

findings: PENDING FINDING 1 (monitor spin on unexpected wait result): REPRODUCED AND FIXED. WinEvent.wait returns -1 immediately when the handle is null, DuplicateHandle fails (handle/resource exhaustion) or WaitForSingleObject fails, and 2 (abandoned) for abandoned waits; any other value is impossible from the native wrapper. The Python loop only logged a warning and kept the event, so _monitor_loop busy-looped with a warning per iteration (the status check does not rescue it when the status event is missing: opens failed). Reachability is low (handle exhaustion / corrupted handle) but the effect is a 100% CPU daemon thread plus log flood. Fix: treat any unexpected result as connection loss (reset events), which gives the existing bounded 2 s reconnect backoff. Proof: test_persistent_wait_failure_costs_one_wait_per_backoff_cycle raised _RunawayLoop (200 stop-flag polls, zero backoffs) before the fix. The first-pass test that pinned 'log and keep the event' was rewritten for the new contract.

PENDING FINDING 2 (stale 'OST active' after silent resets): REPRODUCED AND FIXED. The consumers are service_builder (transaction_monitor.set_ost_status_callback(ost_signaler.emit_status) -> main-thread slot -> conn_manager.set_write_blocked(active) + OST_STATUS_CHANGED -> UiAccessManager._ost_active). _reset_events (WAIT_ABANDONED, exceptions, unexpected results) cleared _status_online without a callback; a reconnect then found OST offline and nothing was reported (state stayed CONNECTED, _check_status_state compared offline with offline), so write connections stayed blocked and the UI kept the stale 'active' value until the next transition (UiAccessManager.refresh() polls is_ost_active() and heals only the UI part). Fix: remember what was last published (_status_published); every status publication goes through _publish_status; a reconnect that finds OST offline, or a failed reconnect, publishes (False) once if (True) was published (conservative: the UI stays 'active' through a transient loss and is corrected when the monitor can establish the truth; delivery failures are logged and retried). stop_monitoring keeps the flag so a restart while OST exited also reports offline.

PENDING FINDING 3 (callback under _debounce_lock): PARTLY REPRODUCED, FIXED. The re-entrancy deadlock named in the finding does not occur: a callback that calls start_monitoring gets False (is_monitoring), and stop_monitoring from the worker thread raises RuntimeError in Thread.join(current thread) before touching the lock (pinned by test_callback_reentering_start_and_stop_cannot_deadlock_the_worker; the real callback, VisualizationService._on_monitored_file_changed, dispatches to the main thread and never re-enters). The REAL defect was different: stop_monitoring's join-timeout branch takes _debounce_lock, which the worker holds for the whole callback, so a slow callback made stop_monitoring (called from the UI thread via stop_database_monitoring/cleanup) block until the callback returned, defeating the 1.5 s timeout. Fix: decide under the lock, run the callback outside it. Proof test: test_stop_does_not_wait_for_a_callback_that_is_still_running (fails with the old block restored in memory).

PENDING FINDING 4 (equivalent survivors / spinning daemon): the two 'equivalent' resets are proven equivalent by a 20,000-scenario differential harness (and the extra operand L213); the 'while True' mutant is now killed by three real-thread tests within 1 s and the real-thread tests are bounded (_BoundedWinEvents raises a BaseException on any reconnect past the expected count; _BlockingCommit raises after 100 waits with the stop flag set), so a mutation can no longer leave a spinning daemon thread. Thread affinity: the monitor never touches EventBus (asserted from the live namespace/co_names); the status callback and notifier messages are invoked on the worker thread and are marshalled by the consumers (OstSignaler.emit_status is a Qt signal emit; QtMessageNotifier.post_message emits a Qt signal).

NEEDS A USER DECISION (monitor): on the very first connection (state INITIAL) with OST already running, _handle_connection_established deliberately announces nothing: no status callback and no 'Realtime Monitoring Active' message (pinned by the first-pass table). The only writer of ConnectionManager.set_write_blocked is that callback, so when the app starts or an Access database is loaded while OST is already running, MDB write connections are never blocked and only the UI (UiAccessManager.refresh polls is_ost_active) reflects OST; if OST is started later the transition is announced normally. Not changed because the intent is unclear; the fix would be to include INITIAL in the announce states.

NEEDS A USER DECISION / low risk (monitor): a notifier or status-callback exception inside _handle_connection_failed/_handle_connection_established escapes _connect_to_events' except block and terminates the worker thread silently (found by the harness: 5/20,000 scenarios 'thread_died'); QtMessageNotifier.post_message only emits a Qt signal and OstSignaler.emit_status too, so it cannot happen with the real collaborators. stop_monitoring does not publish an offline status when it stops a monitor that last published 'active' (UI polls is_ost_active, write block is corrected only by the next connection attempt).

Not reachable by the current UiEventCoordinator flow (it closes the session only after accept), so the fixes are defensive and tested with failing-first tests.

findings: DEFECT (fixed): MdbConnectionManager reused a handle whose rollback failed with a non-08 SQLSTATE when the health probe still passed (AGENTS.md: a failed rollback marks that physical handle unhealthy). DEFECT (fixed): a second failure in the same lease (connection-class error or failed rollback, then a failed cursor close) re-flagged the already evicted handle, leaving a stale id() in _unhealthy_connection_ids; CPython reuses ids so a later healthy handle could be condemned and reconnected spuriously (more ACE client-task pressure). Found by differential fuzzing (seed 72), fixed with a pool-identity guard.

PRODUCTION DEFECT 1 (fixed): a queued mutation whose resource lock is held by another session (SqlInfrastructureError LOCKED from acquire_locks) was delivered as FAILED_BEFORE_COMMIT but then the same plain, non-retryable DatabaseCatalogError was re-raised, so the worker handler closed the session, set DISCONNECTED and ended the worker thread (user must reconnect). The sibling lease path already classifies the same error as a statement-level denial and the writer maps LOCKED to a CONFLICT result. Fix: only retryable/session-expired/credential/read-only DatabaseCatalogErrors and OSError end the session (_is_plain_denial helper shared with the edit path).

PRODUCTION DEFECT 2 (fixed): resubmitting an operation id that is already pending was rejected by PendingMutationRegistry.begin, but delivering the rejection went through _complete_mutation_request, whose REJECTED branch finished the ORIGINAL submission's pending entry and removed its journal record; the worker then crashed on 'The pending mutation is no longer registered' when it dequeued the original and the original callback never completed. Fix: duplicate rejections are delivered through _complete_unregistered_rejection and touch no registry/journal state.

PRODUCTION DEFECT 3 (fixed, high impact): a session whose first polls return remote batches never became HEALTHY. The UI-thread _finish_remote_batch sets runtime.healthy as soon as the checkpoint reaches the feed, so the worker's restored announcement (keyed on healthy flipping False->True) was never fired: the state stayed CATCHING_UP, is_editable stayed False, the writer session was never registered and the permission re-probe never ran (reproduced deterministically with a real worker thread, an asynchronous UI bridge and a feed that releases one change per poll: 'ack 3 hw 3 pend False healthy True state CATCHING_UP editable False'). Fix: the restored state/permission re-probe/session registration are announced exactly once per session generation (new _DatabaseRuntime.restored_session_generation).

Design questions reported, NOT changed: (a) a non-retryable session-expired error from a heartbeat/lease renewal (SqlInfrastructureError SESSION_EXPIRED) ends the worker (state DISCONNECTED) and reconnecting needs an explicit capability re-probe, whereas a local suspension gap reconnects automatically; the tolerant test accepts either design. (b) pending finding (1): a database that never gets a new runtime keeps drain_database_mutations_async pending on retained undelivered cancellations (file unload/reconnect callers have no timeout); pinned as the AGENTS.md retained-metadata behaviour, flagged because a stuck unload is possible in the compound failure 'UI bridge dispatch fails during stop'.

NEEDS DECISION: SqlCollaborationStore.acquire_locks orders application locks by plain ResourceRef ordering (type, id, bid) while SqlProjectWriter._prepare_mutation orders bid resources first. For a mixed request such as {annotation, area, bid, takeoff} the store takes annotation:..., area:..., bid:8, takeoff:... and the writer bid:8, annotation:..., area:..., takeoff:... - opposite orders on bid:8 versus area/annotation, so two concurrent transactions could deadlock (SQL Server then kills one with 1205). In practice sessions start at CHANGE_TRACKING_CURRENT_VERSION() so 0 only occurs while the database version is 0 (== minimum), but test_snapshot_feed_with_zero_checkpoint_reads_from_the_retained_history pins the unverified assumption.

findings: D12 FINDING (defect, reproduced, NOT fixed per decision): classify_pyodbc_error uses substring text rules, so a word echoed in the server message flips the classification. SQL Server's 3960 message echoes the database and table name; a database named 'Permissions_Test' makes 3960 classify PERMISSION_DENIED (non-retryable, read_only_required=True: the session would be forced read-only), 'Timeout_Archive' gives TIMEOUT, 'Cannot open database X' gives DATABASE_MISSING. The numeric echo is already proofed (and pinned by the new tests) but word echo is not; the pin tests deliberately cover only echoes that pass today, the failing reproduction is kept out of the tree so the tree stays green. Reproduction + failing output: SCRATCH/d12_echo_repro.py / d12_echo_repro.out (AssertionError: EXPECTED UNKNOWN, got PERMISSION_DENIED). 3960 cannot currently be raised by the writer (next finding), so the exposure today is limited to SNAPSHOT read paths and any future writer change.

D12 FINDING (reachability): the writer transaction runs at the default READ COMMITTED level (no SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL / SET LOCK_TIMEOUT for writes anywhere in ost_visualizer; SNAPSHOT is begun only by begin_snapshot_transaction for read transactions, connection_manager.py:166). So 3960 and 1222 cannot be raised by SqlProjectWriter.execute against the current code (lock waits are bounded by the pyodbc command timeout, HYT00 -> TIMEOUT, and sp_getapplock timeouts return -1/-3 which become LOCKED, not exceptions); only 1205 is realistically reachable there. The pins hold the behaviour if that changes.

D12 FINDING (availability, not a double write): if the marker query's operation applock is still held by the original writer's transaction (the server has not yet noticed the dead client connection), query_operation waits 10 s and raises SqlInfrastructureError LOCKED (retryable=False, read_only_required=False). _recover_journaled_operations propagates it, so the worker's DatabaseCatalogError handler (not retryable) ends the collaboration worker (DISCONNECTED) and the operation stays UNCERTAIN in the journal until the user reconnects; nothing is replayed. Probe: SCRATCH/d12_locked_marker_probe.py (output d12_locked_marker_probe.out). AGENTS.md says only retryable/session/credential/read-only/OS failures end the worker, so the lock-timeout-on-recovery case may deserve a decision (treat LOCKED during marker recovery as retryable).

(2) Concrete inconsistency: condition folder create/rename/delete and move-to-folder (EP16: EDIT_CONDITION_STRUCTURE is not lock-blocked and the SQL queue_* have no ActiveBidWriteGuard) succeed on a locked Bid over SQL while the Access path rejects them at the service; also queue_projects_delete lacks the Access project-delete guard (moot, only empty projects are deletable). findings: NO USER-FACING REFRESH COMMAND EXISTS: grep of presentation (menus, toolbar, shortcuts, handlers) finds none. UiAccessManager.refresh() and ui_event_coordinator._on_database_capabilities_changed only re-evaluate local UI access; DatabaseCapabilityService has no refresh. What the coordinator treats as 'Refresh' is the DATABASE_REFRESHED event, which is ALSO published after routine post-write reloads (reload_and_notify), compaction, the Access change monitor and external-change reconciliation, not only on a user gesture. Consequence: if a worker ends right after a write completes, the post-write DATABASE_REFRESHED restarts it once (immediate) through the backoff. Bounded (one restart per backoff step) and harmless for credential_required (ends again), but it is a restart without a user gesture; if a strictly user-initiated trigger is wanted, a dedicated event/command is needed (decision for the user).
User Reconnect / Open Files / credential re-entry still call stop_database_async + start_database directly (file_operation_handler, app_controller) and are unaffected by the backoff.

F6 GAP: the message the user sees when the marker query is blocked is 'Another session is resolving the same SQL operation.' (state disconnected); it does not tell them to reconnect, and the worker is silently ended. Pinned as is. Possible follow-up: append reconnect guidance in the LOCKED branch of acquire_operation_transaction_lock or map it in _run_worker. Not changed.

F6 limitation of the model: the strict server answers applock -1 immediately instead of waiting @LockTimeout=10000, so the 10 s stall of the real query before the LOCKED error is not modelled; whether the real server has noticed the dead client by then is untestable here.

A refresh-restarted failed-first-open worker uses retry_initial_failure=True (the handler/restart default), so it retries at the reconnect backoff forever instead of ending after one failure like the original open; unchanged D13 behaviour, pinned by test_user_refresh_of_a_failed_first_open_restarts_it_as_a_retrying_worker.

The mutant 'handler publishes outside the own-event guard' of the first draft was designed away: only one decision point per path remains (the refresh branch either republishes for the handler or restarts directly, never both).

findings: F2 FINDING (mirror choice): Access gates only at the service, UIAccessManager._LOCK_BLOCKED does not contain EDIT_CONDITION_STRUCTURE on either backend; I mirrored service-only and left the UI state alone. Consequence, identical on both backends: on a locked Bid the New Folder/rename/delete/move controls stay enabled and the action silently does nothing (log warning only). Locking the UI feature would be a separate, backend-neutral UX decision.

F2 FINDING (still ungated on SQL, out of this decision's scope; Access twins ARE guarded): queue_condition_create with a folder_uid, queue_conditions_duplicate (including paste-duplicate into a folder via target_changes), queue_conditions_renumber and queue_conditions_update without a folder change are gated only by the UI (EDIT_CONDITION / DUPLICATE_CONDITION are lock-blocked there). The scope pin test documents the boundary for queue_conditions_update.
F2 FINDING (unchanged exposure): the gate is evaluated at submission from the in-memory lock flag; a request queued before a remote lock still executes, as for every other SQL write (D14).

F4-R (not changed): every presentation finish/_on_queued_*_complete that only presents an error dialog (page image, layer insert/rename/move/delete, master-data and cover-sheet finish closures, import, page rename) repeats its dialog if the queue delivered a duplicate terminal. The queue delivers one terminal per operation (interim UNKNOWN/PROJECTION_FAILED are the only extra deliveries, and they are filtered), so this was classified as report-only and left. A central dedupe in UIEventCoordinator.present_queued_mutation_error keyed by (operation_id, outcome_status) would need a new attribute that the many __new__-built test coordinators do not set; say if you want it.

Delivery facts used: SqlCollaborationCoordinator._complete_mutation_request delivers the callback once per terminal; the only repeats are the interim UNKNOWN/PROJECTION_FAILED results and the recovery re-delivery of COMMITTED after the callback raised. Duplicate terminal FAILURES are therefore a defensive scenario (injected), exactly as for D7p.

Behaviour trade-off: ProjectWriteHandler._submit_sql_hierarchy_operation (like the existing ConditionActionHandler guard) now ignores the recovery re-delivery of COMMITTED after on_committed raised. plan_view/window guards only cover non-COMMITTED outcomes and keep the COMMITTED recovery path.

Same-key race of ConditionActionHandler._submit_sql_condition_operation: NOT reproducible. B cannot start while A holds the key; the only way the key frees without A's terminal is a submit that raises, and the real queue_* functions raise only before queueing (validation), so no callback can be delivered later. If a future queue function raised after queueing, A's late terminal would discard B's key; the once-guard would not help (different closures), a key->token map would.

G1 limitation of the detection: MARKER_LOOKUP_BLOCKED is phase based (the marker lookup was refused with no retryable/session/credential/read-only flag). G1: a worker stopped by a stop request or shutdown has no recorded reason and its runtime is removed; a thread that is dead with reason None (not reachable in production) is treated as unrecoverable (pinned by the reason matrix test).

G1: a refresh restart of a MARKER_LOOKUP_BLOCKED worker whose lock is still held ends again at once (the lookup is blocked again): bounded by the backoff, nothing replayed, operation stays UNCERTAIN (pinned with the strict SQL model for both dispatchers).

The ProjectWriteService layer already refuses a locked active Bid at queue time for every command the writer now refuses, except queue_takeoff_placement (rejected when its work runs); the writer rule is therefore new protection only for stale client state (another client locked the Bid) and for the placement. Stage 2 should treat REJECTED+bid_locked like the existing ActiveBidLockedError refusal (silent log, no dialog) and NOT as a conflict.

queue_bids_move is refused client-side for a locked active Bid (decision Q1) but allowed by the writer (move is exempt by resource shape): a stale-state move of a locked Bid by another client succeeds server-side by design.

A Cover Sheet save on a Bid that is ALREADY locked is refused by the writer (cover_sheet/collection children); unlocking is possible only through the 'bid'-only status change (queue_bid_job_status_update), which stays allowed.

JobStatuses.Locked is nullable (YESNO, required=False, no default); the Access writer stores -1/0, the SQL bit stores 1/0; the client reads NULL as locked via serialize_value 'NULL'. The SQL check mirrors that (NULL locked) and inner-joins JobStatuses so a dangling or NULL Bids.JobStatusUID is unlocked.

Ordering of the Violations CTE: bid_locked has Priority -1, so a locked Bid is reported before owner/token/rowversion violations; this ordering is only pinned at text level (the fake does not evaluate ORDER BY).

Edit leases: a refusal returns consumed_lock_tokens=() and never reaches the finish batch, so the transaction deletes no lock row; the coordinator's existing explicit pre-commit cleanup (_release_queued_mutation_resources / _consume_mutation_edit_lease) releases them as for any other REJECTED result.

REPORT (design level, nothing changed): queue_plan_properties, queue_page_settings and execute_plan_properties_local do not validate their update entries up front. An annotation update with an empty uid is still applied by the use case but dropped from the resource list (local), an empty update entry raises IndexError from inside the transaction (local, annotation kinds), and entries without a uid/type are silently dropped from queued resources. The new tests PIN these current behaviours and say so; a decision to validate updates (reject before queueing, like PlanGeometryPayload does for empty identities) would remove the pinned oddities.

REPORT (resolved by an existing invariant): the sp-g1 design finding that DatabaseMutationResult does not enforce 'only a committed outcome carries a value' is out of date: collaboration_dtos.py now raises ValueError for a non-committed result with a value. The value-only commands therefore cannot leak identities from a non-committed outcome (AST #1458 is equivalent). A COMMITTED outcome WITHOUT a value (e.g. recovered after an uncertain commit) is not prevented by the DTO: insert_takeoffs_result, queue_takeoff_placement, both paste routes and save_page_scales now have tests that they do not crash on it.

REPORT (coverage gap closed): queue_conditions_duplicate with reassign_takeoffs had no queue-level test (only the local duplicate_conditions_result variant was in the tables): its dependencies (condition, page, takeoff ownership), the queue-time version capture (captured versions must override the execution-time ones: the optimistic check), its 'Refresh the Bid' refusal and its authoritative families were all unpinned. findings: PRODUCTION DEFECT (fixed, proof-first): sql_server/python/ostv_sql_admin/host_state.py create_wireguard_peer left the freshly written peer record behind when the first atomic_write_private replaced the target and then failed (os.chmod after os.replace): record_created was set only after the call returned. The all-or-nothing rollback now unlinks the record unconditionally (missing_ok=True; the earlier exists() guard guarantees the file is ours).

Design question (not changed): the reference relationship 'BidPlanrooms_BidUID1' names its child table 'BidPlanrooms' while the table is 'BidPlanRooms'. SQL Server resolves it on the default case-insensitive collation; on a case-sensitive server collation 'ALTER TABLE [dbo].[BidPlanrooms]' would fail and database creation with it. The spelling is pinned by tests/fixtures/reference_mdb_schema.json and tests/integration/mdb/test_schema_acceptance.py (it comes from the real reference MDB), so the fix belongs in the SQL renderer (resolve the table name against the model); database_creator pins no collation. Needs a user decision whether case-sensitive servers are supported.

Design question (not changed): LocalDraftRegistry.conflicts_for_changes applies the entity-to-collection overlap only to BID-SCOPED families; a coalesced collection change of a non-bid-scoped family (job_statuses/employees/pay_classes/condition_types/projects collections) conflicts with a draft only by exact identity. sp-g2b judged this unreachable for master data today (those drafts lock the collection resource itself); my sweep confirms the operand mutants survive and I did not pin it.

Design question (not changed): create_wireguard_peer silently ignores an existing peer record that is not a JSON object when scanning for an already authorized address, while render_wireguard_config later rejects the same record ('Invalid WireGuard peer record'); the new peer's files exist by then. The operand mutant (isinstance(existing, dict)) therefore survives; no test pins either behaviour.

tools/audit_sql_integration_environment.py raises FileNotFoundError (traceback) when the backup directory does not exist instead of reporting zero files or failing cleanly; the new test only pins 'never a healthy audit'.
Dead code: common.atomic_write_private calls path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700) after _require_under_private_root already required the parent to exist; harmless, left as is.

The shared test helper environment_support.windows_safe_replace is now itself tested, and the second copy in tests/tools/test_manage_sql_development.py was removed (the module imports the shared one). Both retry only PermissionError on Windows and re-raise the last error after 40 attempts.
Safety net added: every test class of test_manage_sql_development installs forbid_real_registry; without it a forgotten patch of _remove_user_environment would delete real HKCU Environment values.

Over-broad mock (fixed): tests/integration/sql/test_global_condition_scope and test_global_bid_family_scope used a bare Mock() as SqlRemoteChangeReader._reader; renaming or inventing a reader method call survived (demonstrated: _parse_cdn_types and _parse_bid_layers_for_bid renames survived the old double). Replaced by strict_project_reader_double() (Mock(spec_set=names of SqlProjectReader), not an instance of it, so hydrate_connection still takes the general path; the takeoff-only replay path is covered by tests/infrastructure/sql/test_remote_change_reader.py). A new test asserts every self._reader.<name> of SqlRemoteChangeReader exists on SqlProjectReader.

Test-quality issue (fixed): the credential-write guard of FileOperationHandler (authentication mode AND password) was only exercised through the dialog, which blanks the Windows password, so the first pass called its authentication-mode half 'equivalent'; it is observable at handler level and now tested directly.

Test-quality issue (fixed): test_dialog_layout_contract compared the dialog height with layout.sizeHint(), which is only the production height when no label word-wraps at the fixed width (production uses totalHeightForWidth); the oracle now follows the layout's height for the width, so a wider platform font cannot produce a false failure.

Several foh mutants (dropping the permission or collaborator gate, the start_database early return) did not fail but HUNG on a real 30 s open wait (real ProgressDialog + threading.Event); the tests now patch the open step / Event so such regressions fail in milliseconds.

Fake looseness: _database_foundation_support._Catalog.get_database matches the exact name and raises a fixed DatabaseCatalogError (a real catalog also checks state/compatibility and is case-insensitive under SQL Server collation); _SqlDatabaseCreator only raises on create_database; the older foh/Startup tests use SimpleNamespace collaborators instead of autospecs (renames on the coordinator would only be caught by the autospec tests); coordinator callbacks are invoked synchronously or manually, never concurrently.

Qt facts that make tests weak by default and are now handled: a fresh QDialog already reports result()==Rejected (Rejected assertions need an Accepted precondition: added to the connection dialog cancel wiring test), QDialog has no min/max hints by default (button removal is only observable through the helper call), child layouts inherit parent spacing (two explicit setSpacing calls are unobservable).

ProgressDialog._WorkerThread.run does `logger.exception("Worker error")`, i.e. the full traceback of ANY exception raised by the creator/worker is logged; the dialog itself maps non-catalog errors to a fixed safe message and the SQL creator classifies pyodbc errors into SqlInfrastructureError user messages, but an unexpected exception type whose text contains a credential would still reach the log. Not a proven defect (no code path puts a password in an exception) and outside the three modules: design-level observation for the progress dialog / creator.

The same-login refusal (creator and normal-use login must differ, SID comparison) lives in infrastructure/sql/database_creator.py; the dialogs only forward the SqlInfrastructureError text (DatabaseCatalogError subclass). findings: NEEDS DECISION (classification): a plain CONFLICT error that is not an _OptimisticConflict (annotation preflight status 3 'An annotation changed or was deleted', unmapped annotation type, a committed operation id reused for another request) is mapped by SqlProjectWriter.execute to kind SESSION on the DATABASE resource; the conflict publisher turns SESSION into blocks_database=True and UIEventCoordinator then enters the database-wide conflict state (enter_conflict), whereas the takeoff preflight statuses 1/2 are OPTIMISTIC_CONCURRENCY (resource conflict, no database block). The asymmetry (an annotation deleted by another user blocks the whole database until reload, a takeoff does not) is not documented; not pinned, not changed.

The first-pass/sp-g3b claim that removing add_master_data_candidate after an insert in SqlProjectWriter._resolve_global_by_column is unobservable is WRONG: require_unambiguous_incoming_identities treats the same UID twice as ONE candidate, so a repeated identical incoming row passes the preflight and relies on the post-insert candidate to resolve to the first insert. Disproved by WriterMasterDataResolutionTests (global rows and employees); the empty-identity skip argument remains valid.

Design (not changed): in the recovered-marker branch of _execute_mutation_transaction the rollback is unguarded; a failing rollback propagates and the already-recovered committed result is lost (the caller falls back to another operation query). Also the RuntimeError 'cannot switch databases' is raised before the try that records operation_error, so an Access-style caller that swallows it would not be recorded (unreachable: every caller passes the mutation's own database id).

Design (not changed): the validation statement packs priorities into one integer space (ordinal*10+k below 100000, then 100000.., 200000+ordinal): at 10,000 or more request resources the item/bid/child/active-editor priorities overlap the token/rowversion ranges and ties/overtaking would change WHICH refusal is reported (never whether the write is refused; bid_locked at -1 stays first). child_owner (+2) and active_editor (+3) and token_expired (100000)/token_resource (100001) are adjacent: ties would be resolved arbitrarily by SQL Server, so the constants are pinned as text.

Design (not changed): the writer does not bound ChangedFields (nvarchar(1024)) or Payload (nvarchar(4000)) before they go through OPENJSON ... WITH (nvarchar(n)); from memory of the documentation (UNVERIFIED here) lax-mode OPENJSON returns NULL for an over-long string instead of failing, which would silently drop the field from the feed row. No recorder call site passes a payload today (the plumbing is unused); changed_fields are field-name lists.

SqlProjectWriter._is_access_resource_exceeded is unreachable from the shared Access callers: they call _record_caught_mutation_error first, which always returns True, so the exception is re-raised before the hook is consulted. The 'does not retry Access resource error' tests in this module pass because of the record hook, not the access hook (the latter is pinned directly now).

_prepare_mutation fetches from a batch that does not set NOCOUNT (it has no DML today). Any DML added to that batch would front the SELECT with count-only results and break fetchone; the strict fake now models this (opt-in count_dml_result_sets) but the production statement carries no guard.

Strict fake gaps found and closed: refused operation lock answered with session-alive 0 (LEASE conflated with SESSION), hard-coded Exclusive mode, no count-only result sets for NOCOUNT OFF, assert_everything_closed blind to leaked cursors (the lease closes them), catalog check blind to SELECT/ON columns. The same blind spots exist for the other modules that use strict_sql_fakes; the new before-commit open/close comparison and the count rule are available to them.

The T-SQL of the new bid_locked branch is evaluated on sqlite only (logic, NULL/join semantics, priority -1, exemption flag, resource-type exemption); SQL Server acceptance, the bit parameter in `?=0`, READ COMMITTED reads without hints and the Shared-bid-applock serialisation remain UNVERIFIED (as in decisions B1-B3).

Validation SQL semantic coverage is now complete for every branch (item/bid/child owner, active editor, token expired/resource, owned omitted, rowversion, bid_locked): expiry boundaries (>), stale window (>=), session ownership, token casing, priorities, expected-version ordinal mapping, exemption flag; liveness and marker lookup of the prepare batch likewise. A case-sensitive collation is modelled (stricter than SQL Server's default).

TEST-INFRASTRUCTURE DEFECT FOUND AND CLOSED: the three handler test modules could reach a real modal dialog (QMessageBox, ProgressDialog, CoverSheetDialog.exec) when production regressed; in a mutation run this froze the worker process (a native modal loop holds the GIL; the timeout watchdog never fired) and in a normal run it would hang the whole suite. Each module now has setUpModule/tearDownModule guards that replace the handler module's show_critical/show_warning/confirm/confirm_delete_conditions/confirm_multi_delete/exec_with_ost_blocking/ProgressDialog/CoverSheetDialog by functions raising AssertionError; tests that expect a dialog patch it themselves (the nearer patch wins).

DESIGN FINDING (needs a user decision, reported not pinned): ProjectWriteHandler.paste_bids on Access requires `rc == QDialog.Accepted` in addition to a successful _PasteBidsResult (mutants L459 and L480 'drop the rc operand' survive). The earlier draft called the operand unreachable because ProgressDialog._finish_if_ready accepts exactly when the result is truthy. That is not airtight: ProgressDialog.reject() is allowed as soon as the worker result arrived and the thread stopped, so an Esc between the thread stopping and the queued QThread.finished slot rejects the dialog although the paste already committed; the handler then falls through to show_critical('Paste Error', 'Failed to paste bid') and returns False for a paste that happened (and skips on_cut_committed). Narrow race, UX/consistency defect candidate; options: decide success from the result only, or keep and document. Not changed, not pinned.

findings: F1 (production defect, FIXED with proof): a takeoff placement whose submission is rejected before queue_takeoff_placement returns (SQL coordinator _enqueue_mutation/_reject_mutation_submission -> QtCallbackBridge.dispatch is a same-thread direct Qt signal call) was ignored because the pending placement has runtime_generation None until the call returns: the provisional preview, the pending marker and the forward-mutation token stayed forever and blocked undo/redo. Proof before fix: PlanViewActionHandlerSynchronousRejectionTests (4 failing subtests, output kept in scratchpad/sp3a7/proof_f5_before_fix.txt). Fix: _complete_queued_takeoff_placement accepts a completion for the pending operation while the generation is not yet recorded (pending.runtime_generation is None); once recorded, a different generation is still ignored (stale-runtime tests unchanged).

F2 (design-level, needs decision, NOT changed): a queue_* failure other than ActiveBidLockedError (provider missing, payload ValueError, int(bid_uid)) leaves the optimistic state behind in four flows: geometry keeps the pending marker and the moved preview, delete keeps the marker and the cleared selection, paste keeps the cleared selection, annotation insert only frees the token; property edits abort() and placements roll back fully. Probe: scratchpad/sp3a7/proof_f2.py (output: geometry pending ['t1']; delete pending ['t1'] selected []; paste selected []). Pinned only: the forward token is freed (test_a_queue_failure_other_than_the_lock_frees_the_forward_token); P2 covers the lock error only.

F3 (design-level, NOT changed): a COMMITTED paste/annotation-insert result without (or with incomplete) authoritative UID maps raises RuntimeError/KeyError from the completion BEFORE finish_forward_mutation, so the forward token stays registered and undo/redo is blocked for the rest of the history generation (probe proof_f3.py: 'forward tokens left: 1 | can_undo: False'). The placement completion handles the same situation (finishes the token, then raises). The real coordinator always supplies maps, so this is a contract-violation path.

F4 (latent, needs decision, NOT changed): a group/position flush that contains a change whose previous position is empty ([] is what the plan view emits when no before-edit position was captured) next to changes that have one: MDB history registers an entry whose redo raises KeyError (targets built from the old list only), SQL history replays the empty position as the 'old' value on undo (probe proof_f4.py/proof_f4b.py). Reachability from the view was not established.
F5 (cosmetic): on_set_curved passes '' as page uid for a pageless takeoff (all other commands skip empty page uids); harmless because ProjectWriteService drops falsy page uids.

F6 (dead code): the annotation_* branches of _execute_local_plan_properties, the None fallbacks of the _push_sql_*_history scale parameters and the `page is None` branch of _project_overlay_rect_if_current are unreachable (proofs).

F7 (robustness): on_group_rotation_flushed (and _execute_local_plan_geometry) have no guard for an all-empty flush; the real service raises ValueError('A geometry mutation requires at least one update') for it. Not reachable from the plan view today (proof).

F8 (test-quality, fixed): first pass called test_sql_annotation_completion_after_bid_switch_does_not_create_wrong_bid_undo 'sound' but it cannot see a dropped is_forward_mutation_current guard (the real undo service already ignores a push for a non-active Bid): that mutant survived the whole original module and is killed by PlanViewActionHandlerForwardMutationHistoryTests. test_rejected_mixed_move_restores_preview_instead_of_exposing_older_undo is really an access-denial test (name misdescribes it, left unrenamed to keep ledger keys); the first `write = _LockedBidWriteService()` in test_other_deletes_stay_refused... is dead (shadowed by self._handler()). The original named-view colour test was vacuous for the colour (default colour equals the asserted '#008000'); the new NamedViewChoiceTests use a non-default colour.

F9 (fakes): tool_revision never changed in any original test (all tool-revision guards were untested); FakeWriteService accepted payloads the real DTOs reject; FakeProjectData.add_transient_takeoffs delegated to add_takeoffs; FakeUndoService cannot prove history generation/ordering. Closed by the added strict fakes/real-undo tests (see fixture_review).

F10 (design-level, needs decision, NOT changed): with no selected Bid the local branches of on_rotations_flushed, on_annotation_text_properties_flushed and on_annotation_styles_flushed (SQL mode included: `bid_ref and sql` falls through) save through the legacy local writer and register history entries whose targets carry bid_ref None, whereas on_positions_flushed and on_group_rotation_flushed restore the preview and return. Probe: scratchpad/sp4t1/probe_rot.py prints 'rotation_calls [(bid.mdb, [(t1, 45.0)], False)] undo count 1 targets [(None, t1)]' for rotations against 'positions: calls [] undo 0 restored [...]'. Reachability needs get_selected_bid_ref() None while get_current_bid_file_path() is set. Mutant #1214 is the open item of the table below.

F11 (design-level, NOT changed): `_sql_completion_was_applied` only treats COMMITTED results as replays, so a non-committed result delivered AFTER a committed one for the same operation id is processed: in the geometry flow it restores the preview of an already committed move and publishes the pending-state events (differential scen_dup.py, mutant #18: `geometry:C F`). The coordinator contract (one terminal outcome per operation id) makes it unreachable; a stricter rule (any known terminal id is a replay) would remove the hazard.

F12 (hazard, covered by a new test): the request closure of on_geometry_edit_lease_requested aliases the handler's `_geometry_edit_lease_selection` set. After a release (selection change, access loss, authoritative refresh) the cleared alias makes a late grant look mismatched whenever the plan selection is non-empty; only the request-id reset in _release_geometry_edit_lease protects the case of an EMPTY plan selection (sweep survivor L372, killed by test_a_release_forgets_the_pending_request_so_a_grant_for_a_cleared_selection_is_ended). The sp3-a7 draft had claimed this mutant was killed by an older test; against the integrated module it survived.

F13 (test quality): the whole-module sweep of the 457 tests of the sp3-a7 state (265 on disk + 192 staged) left 306 of 2630 mutants alive. 210 were non-equivalent test gaps (failed local writes that still registered history, strict-bool results of undo/redo and helpers, lifetime-target rebinding and the completion callback of queued history entries, Bid/database/Page guards of the placement and cleanup completions, annotation-only and mixed delete paths, paste guards and projection failures, scale fallbacks) and are killed by the 103 tests added here; 96 remain, 95 proven equivalent and 1 open (F10). The sp3-a7 note about the original named-view colour test was confirmed (default equals asserted value); the new NamedViewChoiceTests supersede it for the colour.

F14 (harness): a first-run verdict KILLED with an empty failing-test list is an artefact of a restarted worker (22 cases in 2630); they must be re-run alone before a mutant is counted as killed. Three of the 22 (#1554, #1818, #1824) were survivors in reality; the first two are killed by new tests, #1824 is equivalent (P17).

limitations: No live SQL Server and no sqlite stand-in: SQL queue behaviour, coordinator delivery order and T-SQL are not exercised; results are delivered by hand. Statements about 'one terminal outcome per operation' and 'unique operation ids' are contract assumptions (see equivalence proof P2), not tested here.

test_only_the_cancelled_placement_cleanup_calls_the_exempt_entry_point scans the package on disk (path based), so it cannot be mutation-checked in memory; its positive control is the exact one-caller result.

Mutation harness: persistent workers (fm.py, a copy of the sp3a7 harness that serves mutated source and a SNAPSHOT of the test module from memory, reloads the production module, the test module and tests.integration.history.test_property_lifetimes per mutant, no fail-fast, full failing ids) over 2630 AST mutants of the 5316-line handler. 22 first-run verdicts of the whole-module sweep were KILLED with an empty failing-test list (first mutant after a worker restart); they were re-run alone and replaced (3 of them, #1554 #1818 #1824, were really survivors; #1824 is an equivalence proof below, the other two are killed by new tests). Attribution of the new classes comes from a second sweep of ALL mutants against only the sp4 classes (newk) plus a delta sweep of two classes edited later (newk2); the old tests' attribution comes from the whole-module sweep (full + fix1). Mutants are line-based AST mutants of the working copy at the time of the sweep (handler file mtime 10:05, 2630 mutants, identical regeneration).

Equivalence proofs rest on facts that were checked by script (evidence files in scratchpad/sp4t1: proof_a.py, proof_b.py + .out, proof_scales.py, proof_ast_now.out, scen_dup.py + diffrun_h.out). Proofs that rely on a domain restriction (uids are database identities, never '0', '' or 'None'; the parent uid is str|None; a placeable annotation tool type) say so explicitly; they would stop holding if those domains widened.

FakePlanView's selection_revision bumps on change only; the real TakeoffPlanView bumps on every selection change signal and on clear(). Guard-redundancy proofs (P9) are stated for that invariant; the whole-module differential (scen_dup.py) was run on the fake.

Gap (fixed): the five Hot Link history wrappers (_warn_when_history_view_unavailable) had no test in test_window.py; 6 new tests cover MDB placement/delete/paste and SQL placement/delete plus the wrapper contract (single warning with the exact title and message, re-raise, other errors untouched).

Gap (fixed): the whole MDB (local) flush bodies for positions/text properties (writes, history replay, access-loss restore) and the MDB style failure restore had no test; flush early returns (closing, no writer, no changes, no database path, no view) were never reached with editing allowed (the first-pass tail of test_property_completion_without_history_closing_and_changed_selection ran with access still denied, so it was vacuous: fixed).

Weak tests found and strengthened: test_cursor_buttons_drive_the_plan_view_cursor_mode_and_zoom_commands could not tell a swapped zoom toggle polarity (the call list is identical under the swap because the unchecking fires at the next tool change): now asserted after every step. test_constructor_defaults_and_plan_view_configuration contained 'interval() >= 0' (always true): replaced by timer ownership assertions. test_apply_config_preferences_updates_every_option_and_the_widgets used values equal to the defaults for show_sheet_number and snap_to_pdf_lines_enabled (assignment removals survived): every option now differs from its default. _load_page_content results are asserted with assertIs(False). Exception texts are asserted exactly (regex anchors, exact log messages for the unsubscribe and lease-release cleanup steps).

Design observation (not changed): in _queue_sql_annotation_properties the completion closure holds a strong reference to the window through the restore lambda, so the weakref(window) in that path never yields None; the window-collected guard of the other three operations is reachable and tested.

Design observation (not changed, same pattern in plan_view_action_handler): when queue_plan_geometry/properties/paste/delete raise an exception other than ActiveBidLockedError the window re-raises after finishing the forward-mutation token, but leaves the pending marks, the deferred selection revision and (geometry) a consumed edit lease handle behind. ActiveBidLockedError (P2) is handled completely and tested. Contract unclear, so reported for a user decision rather than pinned.

Design observation: _push_sql_annotation_geometry_history pushes a history entry even when every flushed change lacks an old position (old_changes empty; the MDB path and the property path skip the push); the entry's undo then queues an empty position list. Pinned by DetachedWindowIdentityNormalisationTests.test_geometry_without_a_previous_position_is_written_but_not_replayed (current behaviour: the undo payload excludes such changes); whether the entry should be pushed at all is a design question.
