findings: DEFECT (proven, NOT fixed here: the tool permission for editing production in the shared handler files was denied during this pass; the coordinator or a handler owner must apply it): ConditionActionHandler.on_duplicate_requested's committed_updates(result) (condition_action_handler.py, inside the reassigning SQL branch) does `result.authoritative_result.created_resource_ids[0]`. A COMMITTED duplicate-and-reassign result with no created ids (or no authoritative result) raises IndexError out of PlanViewActionHandler.prepare_sql_property_completion().complete after terminal_delivered was set and the pending marks were released but BEFORE _mark_sql_completion_applied and undo_svc.finish_forward_mutation(history_token): the ForwardMutationToken stays registered, so UndoRedoService.can_undo()/undo()/redo() stay blocked for the rest of the Bid session (AGENTS.md: an accepted asynchronous forward mutation blocks older Undo/Redo only until its terminal result). Proof (kept): sp4t5/proof_indexerror.py with output sp4t5/proof_indexerror_before.txt ('EXC IndexError tuple index out of range', can_undo False, one leaked forward-mutation token). Smallest fix: committed_updates returns None when there is no created id, and prepare_sql_property_completion.complete skips the history push when committed_updates returned None (still marking the completion applied and finishing the forward mutation); regression test to add to ConditionDuplicateReassignmentTests: push_local entry, submit_sql, deliver COMMITTED with created_resource_ids=() and assert no exception, can_undo True again, no placement and an empty pending-operation set. The plain (non-reassigning) duplicate path already guards `new_uids` (test_sql_commit_without_created_conditions_finishes_nothing).

FIRST-PASS CLAIMS DISPROVED BY THE FRESH SWEEPS: (1) test_failed_queued_placement_after_bid_switch_cannot_refresh_new_bid: 'positive control lives in the handler unit tests' was wrong (ids 1384/1385/1404 survived tests.presentation.handlers.test_plan_view_action_handler); closed in CrossSystemPlacementOutcomeTests. (2) ConditionEditorNavigationOwnershipTests.test_real_modal_save_yes_navigation_rebinds_every_condition: the fixture claim 'every dialog is rejected in finally so a failing assertion cannot hang the run' was false (a failure before interact() reached its finally left the modal open and exec() blocked forever; the first-pass sweep recorded 12 TIMEOUT mutants in edit_condition_dialog for the same reason); a 60 s watchdog now turns that into a failure (verified by suppressing the interact timer). (3) RemoteBatchNavigationHandoffTests.test_new_remote_snapshot_after_navigation_still_applies looked like a full positive control but only asserted name/folder/page identity: 18 mutants that stopped the remote snapshot refreshing the other Bid properties survived (closed by RemoteBatchActiveBidProjectionTests). (4) The DetachedScaleWorkflowTests bid-switch test had only 2 kills because its production target (TakeoffPlanView._load_page_impl) was not in any swept file; it is now evidenced there.

VACUOUS-ASSERTION RISKS FIXED: the first draft of ConditionDuplicateReassignmentCleanupTests passed under its own mutant because it replayed the same operation id (PlanViewActionHandler._sql_completion_was_applied ignores a COMMITTED result whose id was already applied, so the second completion never ran); three presentation tests used all()/any() over action lists that were never asserted non-empty (test_inactive_plan_reactivation_keeps_projected_page_state, test_detached_empty_scene_clears_zoom_and_disables_camera_controls, test_main_and_detached_camera_controls_follow_accepted_content_and_recover): non-empty assertions added.

FLAKINESS (tests/integration/surfaces/test_presentation.py): _wait_until is event-driven (WaitForMoreEvents, 10 s bound only for a failing run) and every caller asserts after the wait (_wait_for_scene_colors compares the colours, _wait_for_pages_loaded/_wait_for_renders_idle assert the return value), so a timeout can never pass silently and a loaded machine can only turn a slow worker into a failure after 10 s. The single earlier combined-run failure of test_same_size_and_timestamp_replacement_repaints_both_plan_surfaces is still NOT reproduced (stand-alone 6 more times OK, plus the previous agent's 48 stream runs). Hypothesis: the colour predicate is satisfied by the first render while a second tracked request for the same source is still reading the TIFF, and the test then rewrites the file in place (a torn read or a stale cache insert after the invalidation event). Mitigation applied: _wait_for_renders_idle() drains _pending_page_data/_current_render_requests on both plans before every rewrite. Whether a late in-flight render can repopulate the PageCache after REMOTE_BID_CONTENT_CHANGED invalidated the source is a product question (not proven either way) and is reported for the owners of the PDF rendering service.

FAKE LIMITS PER MODULE (nothing here proves SQL Server behaviour): remote-batch handoff = autospec'd ICollaborationStore/IRemoteChangeReader (return values are unchecked MagicMocks; no Change Tracking epoch/minimum-version, no connection-class errors, no lease loss), plan-property ownership = sqlite stand-in with test-side SQL (no rowcount/NOCOUNT -1, no XACT_ABORT doom, no deadlock/lock-timeout, no rowversion, UID is an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY), duplicate-reassignment/editor-navigation/cross-system/surfaces = hand-completed queue callbacks over a spec'd or recording write service (no server ordering, no UNCERTAIN COMMIT beyond the COMMIT_STATUS_UNKNOWN and COMMITTED_PROJECTION_FAILED results the tests inject). No real Access connections are opened by these modules (ACE limit untouched). Operation ids in the surfaces tests are uuid4 values that are never asserted.

findings: STEP 1, WHAT database_id IS. The word names three different things. (a) DatabaseDescriptor.database_id (domain/entities/database_descriptor.py): an OPAQUE stable id. Access: uuid5(_ACCESS_DATABASE_NAMESPACE, normcase(abspath(normpath(file_path)))) unless an id is passed (saved descriptors pass the saved one); it is a hash-derived UUID string, not a path. SQL Server: uuid5(_SQL_DATABASE_NAMESPACE, database_guid or server|database|auth|username casefolded), or the saved id; also a UUID string. DatabaseDescriptorRegistry (infrastructure/database/descriptor_registry.py) maps _descriptors by that exact id and, for Access only, a second map _access_locators keyed by normcase(abspath(normpath(path))); resolve(locator) tries the exact id first and then the normalised Access path. (b) The RUNTIME LOCATOR that the application passes around under the parameter name database_id (and that BidRef.file_path holds): FileEntry.runtime_locator = the raw descriptor.access_path for Access (the path exactly as the user opened/saved it: never normalised at creation, no abspath/normpath anywhere in the open flow; FileState deduplicates entries by the normalised identity_key, so one spelling per database is registered per session) and descriptor.database_id (UUID) for SQL Server. So for Access the 'database_id' of events, BidRef.file_path, ui_state selected_file_path and write-service arguments IS a raw file path in disguise, and consumers normalise it where they compare (project_write_service.py:2604 and 6762 normalize_path, ui_access_manager 322/332/678-680, descriptor registry abspath normalisation, sql_collaboration_coordinator maps path to descriptor id with registry.resolve). For SQL it is the opaque UUID, compared by equality only (registry dict lookup, remote_change_reconciliation_service.py:55/121/648 'active_ref.file_path != batch.database_id', FileEntry identity uses casefold of it). (c) The MCP server has its own unrelated database_id: sha256(normalised path)[:16] (mcp_server/registry.py:183), never published as an AppEvent.

STEP 1, EVENT PAYLOADS (application/events/app_events.py): FILE_OPENED, DATABASE_REFRESHED, DATABASE_CAPABILITIES_CHANGED, FILE_UNLOADED, FILE_SELECTED and LAYER_VISIBILITY_CHANGED carry file_path (the runtime locator; LAYER_VISIBILITY publishers pass bid_ref.file_path). The rest carry database_id: PAGE_METADATA_CHANGED (project_write_service db_path), CONDITIONS_CHANGED (project_write_service _publish_conditions_changed database_id=file_path for local writes, and RemoteChangeReconciliationService batch.database_id for SQL), BID_AREAS_DELETED (project_write_service:6805), REMOTE_AREAS_CHANGED (page_settings_bar.py:367 bid_ref.file_path and the reconciliation service), ANNOTATION_LIFETIMES_DELETED (undo_redo_service:248 bid_ref.file_path), and REMOTE_BID_CONTENT_CHANGED, REMOTE_HIERARCHY_CHANGED, REMOTE_PLAN_PROJECTION_REQUESTED (+ RemoteProjectionBarrier.database_id), REMOTE_MASTER_DATA_CHANGED published only by RemoteChangeReconciliationService/SqlCollaborationCoordinator from SQL batches (batch.database_id, result.database_id). Rule used for S2: a value that a local writer fills from the caller's Access path is a path in disguise (fixed); a value published only by the SQL reconciliation/coordinator path is an opaque descriptor id (left alone).

STEP 3, OPAQUE-ID COMPARISONS LEFT UNCHANGED (file:function, what, why opaque). detached_page_view_manager.py:_on_remote_bid_content_changed: view.bid_ref.file_path != database_id; REMOTE_BID_CONTENT_CHANGED is published only by remote_change_reconciliation_service.py:377 with batch.database_id (SQL descriptor UUID), and that service itself matches the active Bid with the exact comparison at :55/:121/:648. detached_page_view_manager.py:_on_remote_hierarchy_changed: same, publisher remote_change_reconciliation_service.py:133/230. detached_page_view_manager.py:_on_remote_plan_projection_requested: view.bid_ref.file_path != database_id and barrier.database_id != database_id; publisher remote_change_reconciliation_service.py:410, barrier built in sql_collaboration_coordinator.py:1974/2957 from the SQL result.database_id; the barrier comparison compares two fields of one SQL event. detached_page_view_manager.py:_is_remote_page_data_current and _can_coalesce_remote_page_data: identity.database_id is copied from that SQL event and compared with view.bid_ref.file_path / with another identity's copy. detached_page_view_manager.py:_on_window_scale_changed.complete: current_view.file_path == db_path where db_path was captured from the same view; the callback is only reachable through queue_page_setting_if_sql, which returns None (so no callback) unless the descriptor is SQL Server (project_write_service.py:5851 uses_sql_collaboration_mutations), i.e. an opaque UUID. Internal BidRef-object equalities (_on_takeoffs_changed 315, _invalidate_view_image_sources 520, 844, 856, 888, 1117, 1257 and the exact BidRef check against project_data.get_current_bid_ref() that remains in _on_page_metadata_changed): both sides are runtime state objects built from the same locator, not event/path input; left alone. ui_access_manager.py:322/332/678-680 already normalise.

Mixed handlers: _on_conditions_changed and _on_remote_areas_changed receive both origins (SQL batch.database_id and Access/SQL local-write database_id). normalize_path of a lower-case UUID is the identity (no separators), so normalising does not change SQL behaviour; two SQL ids that differ only by case already denote one database under FileEntry.identity_key (casefold) and DatabaseDescriptor.for_sql_server (database_guid lower-cased).

Reachability, stated honestly: no production path was found where the displayed BidRef.file_path and the event path of the same Access database actually differ today (LAYER_VISIBILITY, REMOTE_AREAS and ANNOTATION_LIFETIMES publishers pass bid_ref.file_path; the three PlanSurfaceAccessContext producers derive both fields from one BidRef; selected_file_path IS _selected_bid_ref.file_path when a Bid is selected). A divergence would need a ProjectWriteService caller that passes the Access path spelled differently from the tree's runtime locator (project_write_service itself normalises before comparing at 2604/6762, then publishes the raw db_path). The fixes are therefore consistency/robustness fixes decided by the user, with tests at the handler level; they are not a reproduction of a user-visible bug.

Not fixed, reported: ui_event_coordinator.py and other presentation coordinators have their own database_id/file_path comparisons (e.g. _on_conditions_changed, _on_remote_bid_content_changed in ui_event_coordinator.py); the identical-pattern rule limited S2 to the two named files, so they were not examined or changed. normalize_path (normcase(normpath)) still does not equate relative and absolute paths, does not strip the extended-length prefix and does not resolve symlinks or short names; not claimed or tested.

findings: Bug 1 root cause: view._element_center computed the on-screen centre of a rotated text as top-left + R(w/2, h/2), i.e. rotation about the top-left corner, while the renderer rotates about the box centre (setTransformOriginPoint(w/2, h/2)) and the model stores the centre; the ost mode returned the stored anchor, so the handle pivot (screen) and the commit pivot (ost) disagreed once the text had a rotation. The handle is created at gesture start with rotation 0 (correct) and re-created at release with the stored rotation (wrong).

findings: Root cause A: a scale change alters Page.overlay_units_per_sheet_inch, which commit 7a1754e added to the render identity; refresh_current_page_overlays therefore returns False and the coordinator falls back to load_page with an identity change, which never preserved the current view and restored Page.zoom_fac/current_x/current_y. Those stored values are only refreshed by zoom actions and right-button pan release, not by scrollbar or wheel scrolling, so they were stale.

Root cause B: the Page object is shared by the main view, the detached view (when no deep copy is made) and the detached window's refresh cache; the view's capture and AnnotationViewWindow._capture_refresh_view_state wrote the detached camera into the shared Page, and the main view restored it.

Regression: git bisect (script bisect_scale_view.py, offscreen, real view) over fc7f470..c9bb334 gives 7a1754e (2026-07-24, 'Fix calibrated overlays and cover sheet PDF indexes'), exact change: 'overlay_units_per_sheet_inch': page.overlay_units_per_sheet_inch added to TakeoffPlanView._build_render_identity. The parent 7a1754e^ preserves the viewport; fe047a0 and 5d7ad08 are already broken and not the cause. The shared-Page write by the detached window came in 92428ec (2026-06-18, 'Preserve detached view camera on refresh') and the shared capture in fc7f470; Bug B only surfaced once the main view reloaded without preserving its view (7a1754e).

Intentionally unfixed: page rotation, flip and size changes (and replacing the image or overlay file) change the page geometry and keep restoring the page's stored zoom and centre (same zoom, same fractional page position, not the same content). No test asserts the resulting position for rotation or size; the flip control asserts zoom and persisted y only.

Same stale-restore defect existed before 7a1754e for invert, bitonal, show mode and flip (verified at 7a1754e^ and fc7f470 with the same script); the fix covers invert, bitonal, show mode and the overlay rect, rotation and deskew keys; rotation, flip, size, image and overlay file changes change geometry and keep restoring the stored page state.

findings: Issue 1 root cause: left_splitter (Conditions above Layers) had stretch factors (1, 1). The Pan handle only moves the outer left_column_splitter, but the nested left_splitter received the whole height change and distributed it by stretch, so Layers shrank or grew with it (Pan 60 px smaller: Conditions +30, Layers +30 before; window height +120: both panes grew). Fix: Layers stretch 0 (setStretchFactor(1, 0)). Persisted keys, hidden-pane size preservation, _ensure_* helpers and the two-pane assumptions are unchanged; with Conditions or Layers hidden the single visible pane was already adjacent and absorbed the change.

Issue 2 profile (real PDFRenderingService, 5477x3651 composite base, 2592x1728 pt page, offscreen): a scroll step costs about 3.5 ms at 1200x800 and 9 ms at 2560x1400 and is almost entirely Qt painting (drawImage of the frame plus the low-res base under it, about 25% of the step; ARGB32 versus RGB32/premultiplied made no measurable difference); there are zero render requests, scene.changed emissions or thumbnail renders during scrolling because ZoomDebouncer waits 125 ms; the Pan sidebar adds nothing (8.91 ms with it, 8.89 without; 3 thumbnail renders in total).

Issue 2 root cause: when scrolling pauses, a visible-frame composite is rendered on the PDFRenderWorker thread. The pdfium and ost_image natives release the GIL (module_pdf.cpp), but every PySide QImage/QPainter call holds it for its whole duration: probe on a 5000x2800 image gives copy 12 ms (GUI loop gap 10 ms), convertToFormat 14 (11), convert plus Darken fill 34 (31), against a pure Python 132 ms loop that only delayed the GUI 19 ms. In the real frame pipeline (invert plus bitonal, 1900x1100 composite frame) the GUI thread was blocked up to 62-79 ms per frame; the worker profile showed convertToFormat (4 calls of 13-20 ms), tint_image, copy, fillRect and invertPixels as whole-image calls.

Fix: presentation/visualization/utils/image_bands.py runs conversion, copy, region copy, invert and bitonal darkening in bands of at most BAND_PIXELS (262144) pixels, writing each band into the result buffer, so the output is byte-identical; images up to one band, indexed images and null images use the original whole-image call. Used by image_effects (tint, invert, bitonal), PageRenderer (pdfium result conversion) and the composite overlay crop. Measured isolated frame (render plus effects): GUI max loop gap 62-79 ms before, 22-31 ms after; the worker pays about 14 ms more CPU per frame (effects 8 ms to 23 ms, render 215 to 255 ms) and the frame arrives slightly later.

Remaining GIL holders in the frame pipeline (not changed): ost_pdf result.to_bytes copies, the Python bytes()/join in tint_image, QPainter.drawImage of the overlay and base into the frame, and QImage allocation; the GUI max gap is still about 22-30 ms per frame. GUI-thread use of pdfium_lock in placement_mode (snap preview) can also wait for a worker frame render in placement tools; not touched.

D1 (fixed) PDF coordinates on pages whose visible box does not start at (0, 0): ost_pdf text runs and path segments are in absolute PDF user space, but the read service converted them as if the CropBox started at the origin. Probe: CropBox [100 100 512 692], line at raw (150..350, 600) reported at page y -8 instead of 92 (outside the crop); MediaBox [50 50 662 842] reported 50 pt off on both axes onto white pixels. Fix: PageCachePdfSource subtracts the visible-box origin from the native page geometry (ost_pdf_writer get_page_geometries visible_box) for text runs and segments. Rotations 90 and 270 were already correct. The same raw-to-page math exists in committed placement_mode snapping and the read server's PDF summaries; not touched (outside the uncommitted scope), reported as suspected.

D2 (fixed) proxy stdio used the Windows console code page (cp1252): any response containing a character outside cp1252 (drawing text such as the >= sign) raised UnicodeEncodeError and ended the proxy; UTF-8 input bytes undefined in cp1252 also ended it, other non-ASCII input was garbled, and a leading BOM gave a parse error. Fix: stdin reconfigured to utf-8-sig with errors=replace, and the JSON-RPC transport writes ASCII-only JSON (protocol _encode default ensure_ascii), so the stdout code page no longer matters. A stdout reconfigure was tried and removed as redundant (equivalent mutant).

D3 (fixed) deeply nested JSON: RecursionError was not caught by the proxy's line parser (process exit) or the bridge's request parser (exception escaping the Qt slot, which the app's sys.excepthook turns into a crash report; the client timed out). Both now return a parse error / invalid_argument.

D4 (fixed) a worker finishing after the bridge object was destroyed raised RuntimeError when emitting its result; the app's threading.excepthook writes a crash report for it. The emit is now guarded and the result dropped.

D5 (fixed) lone surrogates: the bridge encoded responses with ensure_ascii=False plus strict UTF-8, so any string with a lone surrogate (reachable through a sidecar JSON file) raised in the slot and the client never got an answer. The bridge now sends ASCII JSON, and UntrustedText replaces lone surrogates with U+FFFD.

D6 (fixed, prompt injection) sidecar identifiers (level uid, registration page and level uid, assumption uid) were accepted as any string and returned to the AI unmarked and unbounded, so a tampered sidecar could carry instruction text outside the untrusted wrapper. Identifiers must now be 1-128 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . : { } -; otherwise the sidecar is corrupt.

D7 (fixed) a large PNG whose artifact save failed raised OSError out of call_tool (internal error, whole result lost) while the JSON spill already degraded to a preview. It now returns the result with file_saved False and the error text.

Checked without finding a defect: both pipes grant only the current user SID; token compare uses hmac.compare_digest; token is per start, never in argv, logs, responses or exception messages (logs use exception type names only); single-instance guard in main.py stops a second app instance before MainWindow, so there is no token-file race; undeclared commands, unknown arguments, unhashable argument types, path-like page_uid values, tampered cursors (negative, exponent, huge, non-ASCII digits) and non-finite numbers are rejected or bounded; page lookups are scoped to the open bid's model; quantity and coordinate paths are shared by Access and SQL; OST 2D coordinates are a pure scale of page points (user rotation and flip apply only to 3D and export), so page_pts_to_ost is correct; crop caps and invalid crops are enforced; the takeoff proxy has the same stdlib closure (dataclasses, inspect, token) as the shipped read helper, so the shared Nuitka nofollow list is not a new risk; MSI harvests Visualizer.dist, so the copied proxy is packaged.

findings: Follow-up 1 reproduced with failing tests first on the offset-CropBox, non-zero-MediaBox and rotated offset-CropBox fixtures: native ost_pdf text and path extraction returns absolute PDF user space, and every caller that maps it onto the page ignored the visible-box origin. Follow-up 2: the proxy pipe client blocked forever when the app accepted a request but never answered (probe: still blocked after 3 s). Follow-up 3: the bridge now caps worker jobs (MAX_CONCURRENT_WORKERS = 2, counted on the GUI thread, released when the result is handled) and open connections (MAX_OPEN_CONNECTIONS = 8, released on disconnect); extras get busy. A connection without a complete request after IDLE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS (10 s) is answered with invalid_argument and closed. GUI-thread commands are not limited by the worker cap. reviewed_tests.SqlCollaborationOperationTerminalStatusC: Added (decision R3): the terminal set (COMMITTED, REJECTED, CONFLICT, FAILED_BEFORE_COMMIT, CANCELLED_BEFORE_START) and the interim set (COMMIT_STATUS_UNKNOWN, COMMITTED_PROJECTION_FAILED) used by the contract tests must partition MutationOutcomeStatus (a new status forces a classification) and must agree with the coordinator itself: delivering each status through _complete_mutation_request leaves the pending entry, the journal record and the _uncertain_callbacks entry exactly for the interim statuses and removes all three for the terminal ones. Killed: dropping the registry finish in _complete_mutation_request.

Added (decision R3): scenario/property test over 1296 deterministic event orders (7 work outcomes: commit, unknown then committed marker, unknown then lost marker, failed_before_commit, rejected, BID_LOCKED rejection, conflict; x 6 pre-execution events: none, cancel, cancel twice, stop via _reset_session, trust loss, duplicate submission; x 3 projections for commits: immediate, deferred ok, deferred failed; x 4 post-execution events: none, trust loss, late cancel, duplicate of a live id; x 3 callback behaviours: none, raises on first delivery, raises on first COMMITTED; x immediate or delayed dispatcher) against the real coordinator driven synchronously (fakes for store, writer and reconciliation). Records every callback delivery per submission and asserts: at most one distinct terminal status, exactly one closing terminal (a COMMITTED whose callback raised is not closing because the coordinator re-delivers it), nothing delivered after the terminal, only interim statuses (or the re-delivered raised COMMITTED) before it, the write ran at most once (never replayed), the pending entry settles, no journal record or _uncertain_callbacks leak, and the set of observed delivery sequences equals the 18 expected ones. No double-terminal path exists. Killed: dropping the registry finish, .get instead of .pop on the recovered callback, double dispatch of a recovered result, double dispatch of a non-local result, a CANCELLED delivered after the commit result, the duplicate rejection finishing the original entry, no recovery for a failed COMMITTED callback, the recovered not-found status changed to REJECTED.

Added (decision R3): a second submission of a live operation id, made while QUEUED and again while UNCERTAIN, returns -1 and its own callback receives exactly one REJECTED; the original pending entry object and journal record are the same objects, its queue entry stays, the duplicate work never runs, and the original still reports UNKNOWN then one COMMITTED. Killed: owns_pending_entry=True for the duplicate rejection.

Added (decision R3): cancel_queued_mutation returns False from inside the running operation (state EXECUTING), after the COMMITTED terminal, after a CANCELLED_BEFORE_START terminal and for an unknown id, and True (twice) while QUEUED; the cancelled operation reports one CANCELLED_BEFORE_START and the started one one COMMITTED. Killed: dropping the QUEUED-state condition of cancel_queued_mutation.

Added (decision R3): with the delayed dispatcher the recovered-result dispatch payload is delivered a second time by hand after the first delivery; the callback still sees exactly UNKNOWN then one COMMITTED because _complete_recovered_mutation_request pops the stored callback. Killed: .get instead of .pop; a second recovered dispatch.

Added (decision R3): worker-thread scenario. A COMMIT_STATUS_UNKNOWN write whose marker lookup keeps failing (retryable) is still undecided after stop_database; the pending entry stays UNCERTAIN with its callback and only UNKNOWN has been delivered. After restart with the marker readable the same callback receives one COMMITTED, the write ran once, and no entry or callback remains. Killed: dropping the registry finish, .get instead of .pop, double dispatch of non-local results.

Added (decision R3): read-only runtime, operation journal failure, no runtime and a stopping runtime each deliver exactly one REJECTED to the submission callback and leave no pending entry, journal record or queued item. The explicit registry finish in those paths is redundant with the finish done by the REJECTED delivery (mutants removing it survive: equivalent while dispatch is immediate and finish is an idempotent pop).

second_pass.fixture_review: Read the whole coordinator (3,094 lines), pending_mutation_registry, the collaboration DTOs, the real SqlCollaborationStore lock/session/poll semantics and every fake in tests/helpers/sql/collaboration.py. REAL in these tests: coordinator, PendingMutationRegistry, DatabaseCapabilityService, DatabaseSessionRegistry, LocalDraftRegistry, DatabaseConcurrencyTokenService, real DTOs, real worker threads/locks/queues. FAKE: every store (ICollaborationStore), the remote reader, the reconciliation service, the journal, the permission probe and the dispatcher; no SQL, T-SQL, transactions, rowcount, nextset, sp_getapplock waits, deadlocks, SNAPSHOT isolation, identity gaps or collation behaviour is exercised, so nothing here proves SQL Server behaviour. Ways the shared fakes were looser than reality: (1) _LockingStore grants every lock unconditionally, returns a fixed resource from renew_lock and accepts any release (no exclusivity across sessions, no server-side expiry, no stale-session rejection, no sorted all-or-nothing acquisition, no unique tokens) - replaced for lock/lease tests by the new additive _FakeSqlServerState/_ServerBackedStore (server UTC clock advanced only by tests, per-(type,id) exclusivity independent of Bid context, SqlInfrastructureError LOCKED/SESSION_EXPIRED with the real flags, existing-token reuse, release by owner+token only) with its own self-tests; (2) _Dispatcher and the _Delayed*Dispatcher are synchronous, so worker callbacks ran on the worker and Qt/UI affinity and asynchronous projection ordering were unobservable - added _UiThreadDispatcher (queues; only the pumping UI thread runs callbacks) and _ThreadRecordingEventBus; the asynchronous model exposed one production defect (healthy never announced); (3) _DeferredProjectionReconciliation/_FailFirstLocalProjectionReconciliation did not call super().__init__ (no batches/projection_barriers) - fixed additively and they now record what reconciliation received; (4) _CollaborationStore.poll_changes/start_session ignore stop_requested and accept any bid/limit, _RemoteReader hydrates nothing, _RecoverableProjectionStore.query_operation never validates types - covered by explicit scripted stores (_ScriptedStore, partial-batch stores) instead; (5) fake journals never fail unless told to (_FailingPendingOperationJournal). First-pass fixture review verified: ready_coordinator installs an editable runtime without a worker thread (direct _process_* calls), generation 4, session generation 0; I extended it additively (dispatcher/event_bus/polling_policy kwargs, server-backed store registration). Negative-only assertions (assert_not_called/assertEqual(..., [])) always have a positive control in the same test or a sibling.

Records every callback delivery per submission and asserts: at most one distinct terminal status, exactly one closing terminal (a COMMITTED whose callback raised is not closing because the coordinator re-delivers it), nothing delivered after the terminal, only interim statuses (or the re-delivered raised COMMITTED) before it, the write ran at most once (never replayed), the pending entry settles, no journal record or _uncertain_callbacks leak, and the set of observed delivery sequences equals the 18 expected ones. Killed: dropping the QUEUED-state condition of cancel_queued_mutation.

Added (decision R3): with the delayed dispatcher the recovered-result dispatch payload is delivered a second time by hand after the first delivery; the callback still sees exactly UNKNOWN then one COMMITTED because _complete_recovered_mutation_request pops the stored callback. Killed: .get instead of .pop; a second recovered dispatch.

Added (decision R3): worker-thread scenario. Added (decision R3): read-only runtime, operation journal failure, no runtime and a stopping runtime each deliver exactly one REJECTED to the submission callback and leave no pending entry, journal record or queued item. The explicit registry finish in those paths is redundant with the finish done by the REJECTED delivery (mutants removing it survive: equivalent while dispatch is immediate and finish is an idempotent pop).

second_pass.fixture_review: Real RemoteChangeReconciliationService with the real DatabaseConcurrencyTokenService, LocalDraftRegistry, ConflictResolutionService and a real EventBus subclass that validates every payload by constructing the event class; ProjectData is the stateful reconciliation_support._ProjectData fake. second_pass.fixture_review: Second pass of the whole module. The original fixtures built ProjectWriteService against permissive project-data/permission fakes (write_permission_support, write_access_support); their mutation executor ran any operation and returned success, so the 'not committed' outcomes, the exact use-case arguments, the resource/lock flags and the recorded changes were mostly invisible (first sweep: 1672 surviving AST mutants of 2828). I added a strict golden-table harness (_Harness: the real constructor wired with recording use-case probes, a strict executor that, like both real executors, runs the operation and returns a value only for COMMITTED (an uncertain commit runs it but returns no value), a baseline-token fake, a capturing queue provider and a minimal project-data fake) and pin, as literal text, 118 Access commands, 15 Access plan commands, 43 queued commands and 26 queued plan commands, each across denied/locked/conflict/unknown/failure/reload-failed/other-database/equivalent-path scenarios (record lines are sorted because a few commands record while iterating sets; verified under PYTHONHASHSEED 0,3,5,7,17,99). Limits: there is no SQL Server, the fakes do not enforce versions, leases, transactions or rowversion tokens, the use cases are probes (their SQL/MDB behaviour belongs to the use-case and writer modules), and SQL-vs-Access routing is the provider flag only. Remaining unpinned behaviour is listed under limitations.

second_pass.fixture_review: Second pass of import_project_files_from_args_use_case.py: shared fakes in tests/helpers/startup_import.py (FakeImportService, FakeProjectData) are hand-written, accept only the exact positional shapes the use case calls, and the added signature test binds the five call shapes against the real ImportService signatures so a rename or an added required parameter in ImportService breaks the fake, not silently passes. Real: WorkspaceState, FileEntry, DatabaseDescriptor, parse_project_file_args, temporary files, the typed QueuedMutationResult (UUID/status validation). Fake/looser than reality: FakeImportService.queue_project_import always returns a positive id and never rejects or calls back by itself (the queued write service completes via the callback delivered by the test), reload_and_notify returns a fixed boolean, FakeProjectData hierarchy is mutated by the fake service instead of by a real reload; no registry or file-association code runs in these tests (the CLI path is only the parsed ProjectFileArgs). Module-reload note: this module imports the use case module as an attribute of its package; a sweep runner that only pops sys.modules keeps testing the unmutated module (191 false survivors in my first run), so the sweep uses collect2.py which also removes the parent-package attribute. Result: 229 AST + 4 string mutants, survivors proved equivalent or killed (see equivalence_proofs).

reviewed_tests.ImportProjectFilesFromArgsTests.test_sql: Second pass: first file COMMITTED then second CONFLICT: the batch completes only after both, the committed file stays success=True/'Imported successfully.'/project_name 'first' while the conflict keeps its message; tuples (source, target, project) of the queued calls checked. This is the 'earlier committed file stays committed when a later one fails' contract. Agree with first pass. Fake looser: the queue never rejects or reorders.

Second pass: out-of-order completion (index 1 first) still yields argument-order results and a duplicate delivery of index 0 is ignored. Disagreement with first pass: the duplicate arrives after the batch is already complete, where the guard 'if results[index] is not None: return' is unobservable (remaining goes negative and never reaches 0 again); the guard is only observable when a duplicate arrives BEFORE the other file finishes; killed by ImportProjectFilesFromArgsSecondPassTests.test_a_duplicate_completion_before_the_batch_is_done_does_not_finish_it.

Second pass: one vanished source (REJECTED/'File does not exist.') and one queue_project_import that raises (FAILED_BEFORE_COMMIT/exception text) complete synchronously, the batch completes once and counts the rejected argument in failed. Agree. Weak spot closed by new tests: the empty-message default and the logging of the queue failure were unobserved.

Second pass: empty file list completes at once with the rejected args, selected project and nothing queued. Agree. The 'return' after the callback is an equivalent mutant (the loop over zero files does nothing); proof recorded in equivalence_proofs.

Second pass: UNKNOWN and COMMITTED_PROJECTION_FAILED leave the batch pending (no completion), COMMITTED then completes with exact fields, and a late CONFLICT does not complete again. Agree. This is the uncertain-commit rule (never treat an unknown commit as failure); the guard against a second terminal result only shows with two files (see the added duplicate test).

Second pass: UNKNOWN stays pending, a following FAILED_BEFORE_COMMIT completes as failure with the default message 'The file could not be imported.' (the fake result has an empty message) and no project name. Agree.
reviewed_tests.ImportProjectFilesFromArgsTests.test_imp: Second pass: a different checked database precedes the workspace one so the workspace selection must win; asserts target, project, refresh=False, reload once, name from the hierarchy ('Stored Project'). Agree.

Second pass: unknown bid uid gives project None and no orphan flag. Agree; kills the early-return mutants of _project_uid_for_bid.

Second pass: deleted-bids project selection imports unassigned with the orphan flag; the fake service adds a project so skipping the detection guard would make selected_project_uid non-None (not vacuous). Agree.
Second pass: same for a Bid that sits in the deleted-bids project (resolved through the hierarchy). Agree.
Second pass: Access path keeps the synchronous importer: ordered calls with refresh=False and exactly one reload; names are the file stems. Agree.
Second pass: raising import, vanished file and a later success are reported individually; one reload. Agree. Message fallback and logging of the exception were unobserved (added tests).
Second pass: importer returning False yields the fixed message and no reload. Agree.
Second pass: refresh_after_import=False leaves refresh_pending and the pre-import project snapshot, refresh_import_result then reloads once, detects the single new project and is idempotent. Agree.

Second pass: three subTests (no entries, missing file, unchecked file) each produce the 'Enable or store a database' message, rejected arg counted and no flush/import; the sub-cases use fresh services. Agree. assertIn on the message is loose but the exact text is pinned by the added no-target test (no change needed).
Second pass: exact message, flush path and no import/reload. Agree. The orphan flag of a flush-failure batch was unobserved (added test).
Second pass: reload returns False after a successful import: success cleared, exact message, refresh_pending False. Agree.
Second pass: current target (file + project) beats the first checked database; flush receives the target path. Agree.
Second pass: unchecked, unstored and path-less current targets all fall back (subTests), resolve_target(None) too. Agree.
Second pass: current target pointing at the deleted-bids project resolves to project None with the orphan flag. Agree.

Second pass: checked SQL descriptor resolves by database_id (no file existence required), unchecked does not. Disagreement with first pass: assertFalse(use_case.uses_async_import(target)) holds for the fake's default (sql_collaboration False), so it cannot detect a constant False; replaced by a positive/negative pair in ImportProjectFilesFromArgsSecondPassTests.test_uses_async_import_asks_the_import_service_about_the_target_database.
Second pass: exactly one new project is selected and named after the pre-import snapshot. Agree.

Second pass: two imports each adding a project leave selected_project_uid None (ambiguous: never guess) while per-file names stay stems. Agree; boundaries 1 vs 2 new projects are pinned by the added detect test.

Access side: real MdbWriter/MdbSchemaInspector/MdbConnectionManager code over either _AccessTransactionConnections (a recording fake: commit/rollback counters, no mode checks, no pooling, no path locks, so it is looser than MdbConnectionManager) or MdbConnectionManager with a patched pyodbc.connect fake; plus (new) a real Access .mdb through ODBC/DAO in tests/integration/mdb/test_connection_workflows.py. tests/infrastructure/mdb/components/test.fixture_review: All tests run against in-memory sqlite through AnnotationOperationsMixin (the real production class) via two harnesses: tests/helpers/mdb/operations.py (_SqliteAnnotationOps/_ParameterLimitedSqliteOps) and tests/integration/annotations/dimension_support._DimensionWriteOps. Observations: (1) the helpers' _Schema.column_exists/optional_table_missing are constant and _require_write_columns is a no-op, so schema-presence logic is NOT exercised by _DimensionWriteOps tests (tests must create every table they touch; an absent table surfaces as an sqlite error that the production except swallows, which produced one invalid fixture of mine that I corrected); (2) helpers/mdb/operations._SqliteConnectionWrapper commits but never rolls back, while dimension_support's wrapper rolls back, so rollback assertions were placed only on the latter; (3) _DimensionWriteOps._execute_insert_values is a stub that inserts the values dict verbatim (so column mapping is verified but not required-column checks). Verified no mock hides renamed attributes: the writer FakeWriter in the rename test inherits the real mixin and fails if _connection/_schema/_require_write_columns contracts change. No sqlite/Access ODBC dependency: pure sqlite, no gates; Qt only for setUpClass.

tests/presentation/components/plan_view/.fixture_review: Qt tests run offscreen (os.environ.setdefault('QT_QPA_PLATFORM','offscreen') before app creation; _app() reuses the instance). InputHandlerHarness composes the REAL InputHandlerMixin/DragHandlerMixin/SelectionManagerMixin with interaction_support fakes: FakeSceneBuilder (identity coordinate system, records pattern angles), FakeColorService (honours page area selection and inactive color), FakeItem handles. The harness provides its own _refresh_condition_text_labels_for_takeoff (a double replicating the real label recentering), so the label-recentering test proves the drag handler calls it after updating the path, not the real label geometry. _make_hole_resize_view stubs _validate_hole_position/_validate_parent_contains_holes to True; the hole fixture also pre-seeds NoPen/NoBrush on the hole item (setup already equal to the expected value) which hid a mutation until the test set a visible pen first. Attachment tests use test_input_handler._make_view with real validators. Mutation matrix (~30 temporary edits to drag_handler.py, all reverted) now fails at least one test for: skipped vertex validation, winding check removal, missing last-valid update, stale pattern retention, hole cutout style removal, hole/parent validation skips, attachment validity bypass, angle computation, thickness, dimension path/label update/removal, polygon/cloud path update/curve, text pos/width/clip rect, bbox handles/outline, midpoint handles, label recentering. | Read drag_handler.py in full (1080 lines) against every uncredited class (LineLineIntersectTests ... HoleOutlineAndFamilySweepTests, 224 tests): the fixtures are the in-module _DragMath mixin (pure maths, recording _snap_angle), the UpdateDragHandlePositionsTests._view real-Qt harness with FakeCoordinateSystem and scripted linear geometry, and real Takeoff/Condition/QGraphicsItem objects; no Mock/MagicMock is used anywhere in the range, collaborators are explicit fakes or real Qt items, and expected values are hand-solved literals or independently built QPainterPath equalities rather than values produced by the code under test. Risks: Qt boolean path operations treat open and closed polygons alike and de-duplicate coincident lineTo points, and native polygon_is_valid / position_polygon_path already reject <3 points / <6 values, so a set of redundant-guard mutants is equivalent (listed in findings); geometry is expressed in OST/scene units through FakeCoordinateSystem and is not font or platform dependent. A full automatic AST mutation matrix (2134 mutants of drag_handler.py, each run against all 259 then-existing module tests with no fail-fast) was used as the review oracle: every uncredited test fails under at least two mutants, and the 93 surviving mutants were all triaged.

second_pass.fixture_review: Fixtures read: tests/helpers/sql/cleanup_support.py (_WriterCursor/_WriterLease/_WriterManager canned lease: fetchone/fetchall are substring-driven, commits/rollbacks are counters), tests/helpers/sql/strict_sql_fakes.py (StrictSqlServer/StrictRawConnection/StrictRawCursor/ApplockTable/BidLockState/strict_cursor proxies), the module's own _StrictMutationServer, and the new tests/helpers/sql/sqlite_lock_validation.py. WHAT IS REAL: SqlProjectWriter, SqlConnectionManager/CursorLease error classification, DatabaseSessionRegistry/DatabaseDescriptorRegistry, DTOs, resource lock order function, schema (SQL_SCHEMA_V1, CurrentSqlWriteSchema), shared Access-layer write operations, and (new) the writer's own lock-validation and prepare SQL executed on sqlite. WHAT IS FAKE: pyodbc (strict model), SQL Server itself (no T-SQL is executed except the two evaluated statements, translated to sqlite), the finish/preflight/delete batches (text pins only), sp_getapplock (modelled table, scripted codes), rowversions (synthetic counter), identities (scripted), the clock (injected). WAYS THE FAKES WERE LOOSER THAN REAL SQL SERVER/pyodbc, and what was done: (1) the strict mutation server answered a refused operation lock with session-alive 0 (a real SELECT evaluates liveness independently), so a LEASE failure was indistinguishable from SESSION_EXPIRED: fixed, test strengthened; (2) the lock mode of the operation lock was hard-coded to Exclusive in the fake instead of read from the statement: now parsed; (3) NOCOUNT: the strict cursor modelled only rowcount -1, not that a batch leaving NOCOUNT OFF fronts its rows with count-only result sets (fetchone then raises ProgrammingError): added as an opt-in rule (strict_sql_fakes.count_dml_result_sets, enabled for the writer's strict server); (4) assert_everything_closed cannot see a leaked cursor (the lease closes leftovers with the connection): new tests count close() per cursor or compare opened/closed cursors before the commit event; (5) the catalog check validates table names and INSERT column lists only, not SELECT/ON column references: the sqlite tables of the evaluator are checked to use only canonical columns and the writer-vs-schema width/vocabulary contracts are compared; (6) the applock table only answers 0/-1: codes 1, -2, -3, -999 are scripted (not produced by a model of waiting/deadlock); (7) the old per-test SimpleNamespace/lambda cursors ignored execute() and accepted any _get_table_info arguments: new tests use protocol-checked scripted cursors and the real write schema; (8) sqlite is case-sensitive BINARY (stricter than SQL Server's default CI collation), has no locking, no snapshot isolation, no rowversion, no datetime2 precision, and ties in ORDER BY resolve in branch order (tie-breaking is pinned as text). The T-SQL of every statement is UNVERIFIED against a live SQL Server, in particular the new bid_locked branch (UNION ALL member with Priority -1, `?=0`, `statuses.[Locked] IS NULL OR =1`, inner joins to dbo.Bids/dbo.JobStatuses under READ COMMITTED with no hint): its logic is evaluated on sqlite only, its acceptance by SQL Server and the Shared/Exclusive bid applock reasoning are not testable here.

second_pass.fixture_review: Fresh second-pass view of the fixtures. Real objects: the real MenuController (real __init__, MenuBuilder menus and shared QActions), UIAccessManager with its Feature matrix, Config, Page, BidRef, real Qt objects for destroyed-owner paths (QWidget/QDialog/QInputDialog deleted with shiboken delete), QActionGroup. Fakes: window, handlers (recording namespaces checked by a meta test against the real handler/window classes), project data, UI state, capability service, licence and monitor (surface_access_support), dialogs and exec_with_ost_blocking, SimpleNamespace controllers built with __new__ in the older tests. Where the fakes are looser than production: (1) the recording handler fakes accept any arguments; (2) _ProjectData.has_takeoffs_for_pages returns False for an empty list exactly like the real service, so the empty-selection guard of _should_enable_export was unobservable (new MenuControllerSecondPassSweepTests uses a permissive subclass); (3) the capability fake models only database_editable and page locks, not the SQL Server permission matrix; (4) renumber/delete availability come from handler fakes, so EDIT_CONDITION_STRUCTURE lock blocking is not projected through the menu here (the menu itself never queries that Feature; it is verified in the UIAccessManager and UIEventCoordinator modules); (5) shiboken isValid(stub) and isValid(None) are True, so destroyed-owner tests use real Qt objects and the isValid-patched tests are not destroyed-owner tests. Every one of the 123 existing tests was read against the production code before the first-pass note was consulted; no disagreement. Mutation: 971 AST mutants of menu_controller.py in memory (fastmut2 with modal QMessageBox helpers stubbed to raise). The in-memory patcher cannot apply mutants to module-level set literals, so 8 string-constant mutants of _TAKEOFF_SCOPED_VARIABLE_KEYS were run with mutrun.py and are all killed.

tests/presentation/components/test_mesh_.fixture_review: Checked tests/presentation/components/mesh_support.py (FakeMeshScene/FakeMeshCamera/FakeMeshRenderer/FakePickingMeshRenderer/FakeMeshSignal/FailingInitializationRenderer) and the module-local _Renderer/_Signal/_Screen/_Window/_Timer doubles against production mesh_view.py. Fakes mirror the native Scene/Camera/Renderer surface actually called by OpenGLViewer (scene.clear/add_mesh/empty/get_bounds/selection, camera.reset/show_object/restore_state/rotate/pan/has_velocity, renderer.suspend/resume/clear_frame/set_plan_texture/pick). _make_page_plane_viewer builds an OpenGLViewer via __new__ and sets every attribute the exercised paths read; added a scene_content_changed recorder there so emissions are observable. Real native ost_renderer.Camera/MeshData/Box3 are used where inertia and mesh conversion matter. The three real-widget classes create real Qt windows and patch only _ensure_renderer. Found a real fixture defect: MeshViewNativeSurfaceOwnerTests never created a QApplication (it ran first alphabetically), so running the module alone hard-crashed the interpreter (0xC0000409) instead of failing; fixed by creating the app in the test and dropping the cross-test import of tests.integration.selection.area_routing_support. Found a swallowed-AssertionError pattern (patch side_effect=AssertionError inside code guarded by except Exception) in cleanup test; replaced by assert_not_called. Ran ~70 single-line production mutations against the module (script in scratchpad); remaining survivors are equivalent/defense-in-depth lines (redundant hidden-surface guards layered with resume_rendering, disconnect-then-connect dedupe, accepted-bid None check subsumed by the != check), timer disconnect hygiene in cleanup, and setters/wheel/delete-key paths outside the assigned tests.

second_pass.fixture_review: Second pass of the module's 352 original tests (every test read in full, notes of the previous pass kept) plus review of the 1063 tests added in this task. Fixtures: coordinators are built with UIEventCoordinator.__new__ and explicit recording fakes/SimpleNamespace objects so a renamed production attribute raises; the constructor test (Sp3a5aConstructionTests) builds the real UIEventCoordinator with a real EventBus and real Sidebar/Viewer/Toolbar/Placement coordinators. Where Mock is used it is Mock(spec=...) (ToolbarStateCoordinator, SidebarCoordinator, ViewerSyncCoordinator) or an explicit method list; the two bare-Mock tests named by the previous pass were strengthened with spec'd doubles and positive controls. Ways the fakes are looser than real SQL Server / production: (1) there is no SQL Server: results are pre-classified QueuedMutationResult/EditLeaseResult objects, so rowcount (-1 under NOCOUNT), nextset, XACT_ABORT dooming, connection-vs-statement error classes, deadlock/timeout, uncertain commit, sp_getapplock codes and rowversion checks are not modelled; the COMMIT_STATUS_UNKNOWN/COMMITTED_PROJECTION_FAILED/REJECTED(bid_locked) branches are driven by hand-built DTOs. (2) fake write services accept any signature unless a test binds it with inspect.signature (the dialog openers and recording stubs of the new tests do); SharedDoubleContractTests only pins the shared doubles and FakeViewer lacks update_license_plan_state. (3) request_local_edit/queue_* fakes invoke callbacks synchronously, while production delivers them from the worker through QtCallbackBridge, except where tests defer the callback or spin the Qt loop (BidLockedRejection tests, late lease grants). (4) FakeViewer-style doubles accept every remote Plan update; stale runtime generation and viewer rejection are exercised only by the new RemoteProjectionBarrier tests (real barrier/token, fake viewer returning accepted=False or raising). (5) ImmediateNavigationOperations completes bid loads synchronously. (6) dialogs, ModalEditLeaseSession, exec_with_ost_blocking, show_warning/show_critical are replaced at the coordinator module so no modal can hang; real dialog behaviour is covered by the dialog test modules (real BidAreasDialog/SetScaleDialog/AdjustImagesDialog/RenamePageDialog + real ModalEditLeaseSession are used only in the locked-Bid draft/lease tests). (7) Qt runs offscreen; QTimer.singleShot(0) is driven with processEvents. Production-as-oracle risks reviewed: expected values in the new tests are literals or recorded call logs; the only production-computed oracle is the module's own _mesh_geometries_to_render_buffers in the native-scene tests, whose output is compared with an independently built expectation.

second_pass.fixture_review: Real PySide6 widgets (offscreen) and the real SqlConnectionDialog/SqlConnectionFormMixin/SqlConnectionDialogResult; the only fakes are the icon providers (RecordingIconProvider records the iconed widgets; a few older tests use a bare type()/Mock() provider that accepts any call, which is harmless because set_window_icon is asserted only where it matters) and show_warning, replaced for the whole module by NoModalWarnings (tests/presentation/dialogs/sql_dialog_support.py). That helper patches the name in BOTH dialog modules with a recorder lambda(parent, title, message): production calls show_warning with exactly three positional arguments so the recorder is as strict as the real function for these calls, and an unexpected warning fails an assertion on shown_warnings instead of blocking on a QMessageBox; its form_rows/margins helpers are pure readers of the Qt layouts (production never uses them, so they are not an oracle) and every caller asserts exact lists so an empty loop cannot pass. The helper itself is stricter than needed in one way and looser in none that matters. No SQL Server is involved at all: this dialog never connects; it only validates the form and returns a SqlConnectionDialogResult, so SQL fidelity (rowcount/NOCOUNT, XACT_ABORT, applock codes ...) is not applicable. Real: Qt widgets, signals, dataclasses, SqlServerDatabaseLocation. Fake: icon provider, show_warning. Qt specifics a reader must know: a fresh QDialog already reports result()==Rejected, so Rejected assertions are only meaningful after an Accepted precondition (added to the cancel wiring test in this pass); child layouts without an explicit spacing inherit the parent layout's spacing (proved in sp3a2/proof_spacing_repr.py), which makes the explicit setSpacing on the authentication and credential layouts unobservable; the two radios are an exclusive group so each toggle fires both toggled signals (proved exhaustively in sp3a2/proof_radio.py), which makes either toggled connection redundant on its own. Second pass added a sentinel-password test (warnings, reprs, labels, tooltips, descriptor JSON, dialog repr) and a direct _apply_connection test (both authentication directions, lock flag), and strengthened the cancel wiring and idempotent reject tests.

second_pass.fixture_review: Real SqlDatabasePropertiesDialog/SqlConnectionFormMixin/SqlConnectionDialog (offscreen Qt), real dataclasses (SqlServerDatabaseLocation, SqlDatabasePropertiesResult, SqlDatabaseRuntimeCredentials, SqlDatabaseCreationResult), real ProgressDialog + QThread in four tests (test_create_mode_initializes_before_accepting, the worker-responsiveness test and the new real-worker cleanup test use the real worker thread and nested event loop; the contract classes use a synchronous _RecordingProgressDialog stand-in whose exec() optionally runs a hook BEFORE the task, which models 'owner changed before/during the setup'). Fakes: _database_foundation_support._Catalog (exact-name get_database, raises DatabaseCatalogError for an unknown name; looser than a real catalog, which also checks state/compatibility and is case-insensitive under SQL Server collation), _SpyCreator (records the real create_database_for_client signature; _SqlDatabaseCreator only raises if create_database is called), bare Mock()/Mock creators in the older tests (accept any call but are always asserted through call_args or assert_not_called on the one method that matters), _IconProvider/RecordingIconProvider, show_warning (NoModalWarnings recorder or an explicit patch asserted with the exact (parent, title, message)). tests/presentation/dialogs/sql_dialog_support.py helpers are pure Qt readers (not an oracle for production). No SQL Server and no pyodbc exist here: the dialog never talks SQL itself, it hands a location+password to the catalog/creator, so rowcount/NOCOUNT/XACT_ABORT/applock/Change Tracking fidelity is not applicable; where the real creator matters (same-login refusal, SID comparison) the repo has tests/integration/sql/test_creation_identity.py and tests/infrastructure/sql/test_database_creator.py with scripted connections. The creator's SqlInfrastructureError text is simply forwarded by the dialog (DatabaseCatalogError subclass) and the dialog trusts the creator to sanitise it; anything else becomes a fixed safe message (raise ... from None, __cause__ and __context__ proven None). Qt facts used: a fresh QDialog reports Rejected so Rejected assertions need an Accepted precondition; child layouts inherit the parent spacing; the two radios are an exclusive group. Second pass found three non-AST mutants that survived every pre-existing test (worker closure reading self._database_creator instead of the captured creator; progress callback bound to a different ProgressReporter than the dialog listens to, twice) and one dead-code mutant (database_combo.clear() in _populate_databases): all four now have killing tests (cleaned-up-owner assertion on calls, reporter identity, repopulation test). Added a real-thread cleanup-during-setup test, four sentinel-password tests (warnings, reprs, labels, descriptor JSON, exception chain) and the same-login refusal display test.

second_pass.fixture_review: Second pass of condition_action_handler.py and its tests. First-pass fakes: SimpleNamespace coordinators/services (strict: a missing attribute raises), real ConditionsSidebar, real EditConditionDialog and Layers dialog in several tests, real UIEventCoordinator.present_queued_mutation_error and a real SqlCollaborationCoordinator in the B4/G4 tests. The added tests use one strict recording harness (_SecondPassConditions): every service call is recorded with exact arguments, Access results are scripted per method, queued callbacks are kept and delivered by the test, every coordinator side effect lands in one ordered event list, the lease owner grants synchronously and records requests and ended handles, and the condition dialog class is a recording fake so every constructor argument is asserted (first-pass tests never asserted how the dialog is wired per backend). Looser than reality: no live SQL Server; the queue fake never rejects asynchronously or reorders; leases are granted synchronously and never lost by a server; the real EditConditionDialog behaviour is only covered in the first-pass tests that build it. Not covered here: the plan reassignment branch of on_duplicate_requested (needs the real plan view; its commit paths are exercised in tests/integration/conditions/duplicate_reassignment); see equivalence/limitation notes for the mutants that remain. Module guard added: setUpModule makes show_warning, confirm, confirm_delete_conditions, confirm_multi_delete and exec_with_ost_blocking of the handler module raise AssertionError unless a test patches them (the earlier thread-based mutation runner froze on real Qt widgets and dialogs). Mutation: AST+string sweep (1298+139 mutants) with the main-thread collect2.py runner: first-pass tests left 627 AST + 102 string survivors; results of the final run are in the findings table. SECOND SESSION (sp4-t4): the survivors of the previous four rounds (147 of 1437 mutants) fell into three groups: (1) the Plan duplicate-and-reassign branch (SQL and Access) which the earlier rounds left to the integration suite, (2) guards that need an input the shared harness never produced (no write service, empty selections, no sidebar, a folder or Bid changing during a create save, a saved uid missing from the authoritative family), (3) provably equivalent mutants. Group 1 is now exercised through two recording fakes (a QObject Plan stand-in with the (token, page) context-menu owner, selection/tool revisions and a current page, and a Plan-view handler recording prepare_sql_property_completion/record_local_condition_reassignment); they are NOT the real Plan view, so the real completion semantics stay covered by the plan-view handler tests and tests/integration/conditions. Looser than reality: shiboken delete() of a Python QObject subclass keeps its Python attributes readable (the real PlanView attributes behave the same), isValid(None) is True in shiboken (a production truthiness guard depends on it), and the queue fake never reorders or delivers asynchronously. Final state: 36 mutants survive, all with an equivalence argument in equivalence_proofs.

second_pass.fixture_review: Second pass of cover_sheet_handler.py and its tests. Fakes: SimpleNamespace/handwritten classes for project data, read/write services, access manager and the lease owner (the lease owner always grants immediately and calls back synchronously, so no delayed-grant ordering is covered here), _FakeCoverSheetDialog from tests/presentation/dialogs/cover_sheet/path_support.py (records only the async save callables, so every other constructor argument of the handler->dialog wiring was unobserved by the first-pass tests), strict fakes that raise (self.fail / AssertionError) when an unexpected method is called. Real: CoverSheetHandler, CoverSheetContext, ModalEditLeaseSession, EventBus, the typed DTOs (QueuedMutationResult validation) and, in the lock-refusal tests, the real CoverSheetDialog and the real UIEventCoordinator.present_queued_mutation_error. Fixture that already held the expected value: test_unlocked_sql_cover_sheet_invokes_async_save returned data.job_statuses from the snapshot fake, so deleting the handler's SQL assignment of the snapshots survived (fixed by the new harness whose snapshots are distinct objects compared by identity). Looser than reality: no live SQL Server; the queue fake never rejects asynchronously and never reorders; leases are not server-enforced. Module guard added (setUpModule): show_critical, confirm, exec_with_ost_blocking and CoverSheetDialog of the handler module raise AssertionError unless a test patches them, so a regression that reaches a real modal dialog fails fast instead of freezing the process. In-memory AST+string sweep (332+87 mutants) with collect2.py: first-pass tests alone left 123 AST + 27 string survivors; with the added tests 5 remain, 2 of them proved equivalent and 3 killed by strengthening assertFalse to assertIs(..., False).

second_pass.fixture_review: Real FileOperationHandler everywhere (never mocked), real DatabaseDescriptorRegistry, real DatabaseDescriptor/FileEntry/FileStateAggregate/JsonFileStateRepository (new tests), real Qt widgets for the owner window and for every destroyed-owner test. Fakes: in-memory file-state models (_FlowState records every save and can fail chosen saves; many older tests use ad-hoc State classes), dialog stand-ins (_flow_dialog/_Dialog/_MaintenanceDialog/_Properties: OpenFilesDialog and SqlDatabasePropertiesDialog are replaced by patching the module name), synchronous ProgressDialog stand-ins, and signature-enforcing create_autospec collaborators (SqlCollaborationCoordinator, DeferredPersistenceManager, UIAccessManager, FileLoadingService, DatabaseMaintenanceService, ICredentialStore, IDatabaseCatalog, ISqlDatabaseCreator, EventBus), shared per process by _shared_autospec and fully reset on each use. The older Startup/Cleanup tests use SimpleNamespace collaborators that accept only the lambda signature they define (not spec'd to the coordinator, so a renamed production method on those would only be caught by the autospec-based tests). IMPORTANT Qt fact: shiboken6.isValid(None) and isValid(<non-Qt stub>) return True, so every test that builds the handler with window=None or a Python stub dialog can never reach the destroyed-owner branches; the real-widget tests (test_open_files_return_tolerates_destroyed_parent, test_a_destroyed_window_or_dialog_*, compaction context-change tests, creation destroyed-owner tests, test_a_window_destroyed_during_the_open_wait_*) cover them. The same window=None limitation made the PARENT of 23 show_warning calls invisible: all 23 `show_warning(self.window, ...)` -> None mutants survived the whole module; the flow fixture now records every warning parent and asserts in tearDown that it is the owning window, and FileOperationHandlerWarningOwnerTests drives the eight remaining startup-test-only warnings through the real window. No SQL Server and no pyodbc is involved: the handler only talks to the coordinator/credential store/registry through the interfaces, so SQL fidelity items (NOCOUNT, XACT_ABORT, applock, change tracking ...) do not apply; the coordinator's drain/stop/start semantics are modelled by recorded callbacks and are therefore only as faithful as those fakes (a real coordinator may call the callback on a worker or later; tests invoke callbacks synchronously or manually after the handler returned, which covers 'late' completions but not true concurrency). Credential store: fake in-memory dict (real Windows Credential Manager is covered by the credential store tests). There are no native QFileDialog calls in this handler; its nested event loops are OpenFilesDialog.exec, SqlDatabasePropertiesDialog.exec, ProgressDialog.exec and the confirm() box; their continuations re-check isValid(window)/isValid(dialog), the maintenance target identity (now also against an EQUAL but replaced entry) and the access permission. Second pass additions: owner-parent assertions, replaced-by-equal-entry cases, real file_state.json (password never persisted, DatabaseGuid identity), failure warnings with sentinel passwords, release-chain (finally) tests, fast-failing patches so that mutants reaching a real 30 s open wait no longer hang the suite.

reviewed_tests.PlanViewActionHandlerSynchronousRejectio: Added (second pass): proof test for production fix F1. The SQL coordinator rejects an unqueueable submission through the Qt callback bridge, i.e. the completion runs BEFORE queue_takeoff_placement returns, when the pending placement still has runtime_generation None. The fake service completes synchronously with generation 0 and 3 (both must work); the test asserts the exact single WARNING text, no model takeoff left, no pending marker, no pending placement, no forward-mutation token and no history. Before the fix the completion was ignored and all of that stayed behind (output kept in scratchpad/sp3a7/proof_f5_before_fix.txt).

Added (second pass): same synchronous rejection against the REAL UndoRedoService holding one earlier entry: a leaked forward-mutation token would make can_undo() False (undo blocked until terminal); the assertion is the positive control that the earlier entry stays undoable.

Added (second pass): the same synchronous path with the real locked_bid_refusal_result (BID_LOCKED rejection): assertNoLogs WARNING (a refusal the user already saw is not logged), and the preview, marker and token are still cleaned up. Positive control is the non-locked sibling above that asserts the exact warning.

Added (second pass): guards the opposite direction of the F1 fix: once queue_takeoff_placement returned and the generation is recorded, a REJECTED result of another runtime generation must still be ignored (preview and pending placement kept, recorded generation unchanged). Without it the relaxed generation check could be widened to accept any generation.

Added (second pass): pure static helper with falsy values ('' None 0) and duplicates in the middle; expected list is a literal that fixes both de-duplication and first-seen order.

reviewed_tests.PlanViewActionHandlerLeaseReleaseAndOver: Added (second pass): sweep survivor L372 (`_release_geometry_edit_lease` no longer clears the request id). The pending lease request is released by an empty selection change; the request closure aliases the handler's selection set, which the release clears, so a late grant only looked mismatched because the plan selection was non-empty. With an empty plan selection the cleared alias equals it and, without the request-id fence, the late grant would be ADOPTED for an empty selection. Asserts the id is empty after the release, the late grant is ended exactly once and nothing is stored or marked granted/pending.

Added (second pass): positive control of the lease test above: the same request and grant with an unchanged selection is adopted (handle stored, selection marked granted, request id cleared, no lease ended), so the release test cannot pass because grants are never adopted.

second_pass.fixture_review: Second pass of the fakes. REAL in this module: PlanViewActionHandler, AnnotationWriteCoordinator, SelectionClipboardService (copy tests), the DTOs (QueuedMutationResult with its UUID/rejection-reason/commit_attempted rules, EditLeaseHandle/Result/Loss/ResourceLock, ResourceRef, PlanItemsPastePayload with its alignment/uniqueness rules, InsertTakeoffSpec, and in the added strict fake PlanGeometryPayload/PlanPropertyPayload/PlanItemsDeletePayload), Takeoff/BidAnnotation/Condition entities, the real UndoRedoService (about 25 tests: forward-mutation tokens, history generation, submission order, can_undo/can_redo), the real ProjectWriteService only in test_the_real_service_queues_the_handlers_cleanup_on_a_locked_bid (through the fake provider/executor of tests.application...test_project_write_service._Harness) and real Qt for dialogs and destroyed widgets. FAKE: FakePlanView (hand-written, unspecced), FakeProjectData, FakeWriteService, FakeAnnotationWriteService, FakeUndoService, FakeEventBus, FakeClipboard, FakeAccess, FakeUiState. No SQL Server and no sqlite are involved: the SQL queue is a recorder whose results are delivered by hand (never synchronously from inside queue_*), so nothing here proves server or T-SQL behaviour; the coordinator contract (one terminal outcome per operation id, interim UNKNOWN/PROJECTION_FAILED first) is assumed, not exercised. Ways the fakes are looser than the real objects (checked with inspect/AST against ProjectWriteService, UndoRedoService and the plan view): (1) FakeWriteService.queue_* accepts empty payloads, unknown kinds, non-numeric Bid uids and non-serialisable updates that the real service rejects (PlanGeometryPayload requires one update, PlanPropertyPayload JSON, int(bid_uid)); it never raises ActiveBidLockedError (only _LockedBidWriteService does), returns a constant runtime generation 3 and never validates edit-lease ownership; its parameter names differ from the real ones in several signatures (specs/takeoff_specs, uids/takeoff_uids ...), harmless only because the handler passes them positionally. The added _PayloadValidatingWriteService builds the real DTOs first and the module now proves every SQL entry point and every history replay passes them. (2) execute_plan_geometry_local/execute_plan_properties_local apply writes one after another and stop at the first failure without rollback (the real MDB executor is one transaction, and rejects an all-empty geometry payload with ValueError), and the plain fake drops page_uids/dependency_resources of the property executor (added _OptionRecordingWriteService records them); the handler only projects after COMMITTED, which is what is verified. (3) FakeUndoService runs undo/redo callbacks synchronously on demand, bind_latest_history_to_forward_mutation is a no-op and is_forward_mutation_current is true until finish: it cannot prove history generation, ordering or blocking (the real-undo tests, mostly new, do). (4) FakePlanView.set_selected_uids bumps selection_revision only on change like the real view, but tool_revision was a constant never changed by any test (now bumped by the added tool-revision tests), there is no resolve_pasted_child_parents (added _ParentResolvingPlanView), no signals (added _SignalRecorder wiring test), and shiboken isValid() is True for plain objects, so destroyed-owner branches are only reachable with a real QWidget. (5) FakeProjectData.add_transient_takeoffs delegates to add_takeoffs (added _TransientRecordingData distinguishes them); the same page objects are returned until a test replaces the SimpleNamespace page, so page-identity guards depend on those replacements. (6) FakeClipboard/FakeAccess/FakeUiState are mutable doubles; FakeUiState returns a constant Bid ref (tests monkeypatch get_selected_bid_ref). The fakes are shared by 11 other test modules; nothing shared was changed, new behaviour lives in subclasses added at the end of this module. sp4 additions: the sweep drove the fakes harder and found where they were too permissive. New helpers (all in this module, shared fakes untouched): _RecordingHistory (keeps the submit callables of the latest queued history entry so a test can complete them with its own `done` callback, and records announced annotation deletions), _BackoutRecordingPlanView (remembers the conditions handed to a Backout paste), and uses of the existing _TransientRecordingData, _ParentResolvingPlanView, the real UndoRedoService (queued placement history in the real service) and a real QDialog subclass that deletes its C++ object inside exec() (destroyed picker). Looseness that hid the survivors: FakeUndoService.bind_latest_history_to_forward_mutation is a no-op and its undo/redo lambdas swallow the `done` callback, so a dropped `done(result)` in a queued history entry was invisible until _RecordingHistory/the real service drove it; FakeWriteService.execute_plan_items_*_local always report COMMITTED (and the fake delete never projects into FakeProjectData), so refused-write and projection-failure branches needed per-test overrides (execute_plan_items_delete_local, reload_and_notify, uid_batches); FakePlanView.set_selected_uids bumps the selection revision only on change like the real view but a test can assign `selected` directly (used on purpose to simulate a view that lost the selection without a revision bump); the plain FakeProjectData accepts any page uid and never removes annotations on a queued delete (so same-batch exclusion and 'stale model at capture time' paths needed explicit setup); FakeUiState returns a constant Bid and tests replace _ui_state with SimpleNamespace objects (a Bid of the same database with another uid, the same uid in another database, and None are the three cases the placement/cleanup guards distinguish). The fakes remain looser than the real SQL path: no coordinator, no sqlite stand-in, no real DTO validation except where the strict fakes build them, and nothing here proves server or T-SQL behaviour.

second_pass.fixture_review: Second pass of project_write_handler.py and its tests. First-pass fakes (tests/presentation/handlers/project_command_support.py: _FakeDeferredPersistence variants that only flush after the matching cancel, _MoveToDeletedWriteService, _QueuedHierarchyDeleteWriteService, _DeleteBidUiState, _PartialPasteWriteService) are hand-written and mirror production signatures; several tests use real UIStateManager, ProjectDataService, HierarchyData, QWidget (destroyed with shiboken.delete) and the real SqlCollaborationCoordinator (G4 tests) and the real UIEventCoordinator.present_queued_mutation_error (B4 tests). The added tests use one strict recording harness (_SecondPassHierarchy): every write-service call is recorded with exact positional and keyword arguments, Access results are scripted per method, queued callbacks are kept and delivered by the test, selection changes are an ordered list, and the Qt progress dialog is replaced by a fake that runs the task, records busy flag and progress texts and returns the scripted result code (never a worker error with a result). Looser than reality: no live SQL Server (the queue fake never rejects asynchronously, never reorders, and a granted callback is delivered synchronously by the test); ProgressDialog accepts any truthy result (a _PasteBidsResult is always truthy, so rc is Rejected only for a worker error with a None result), which the fake harness reproduces only for the worker-error case. Module guard added: setUpModule makes show_critical, show_warning, confirm and ProgressDialog of the handler module raise AssertionError unless a test patches them (a first AST sweep froze its worker processes on unpatched QMessageBox calls: a regression there hung instead of failing). Mutation: AST+string sweep (690+95 mutants) with collect2.py in the main thread: first-pass tests leave the survivors listed in survivors_killed; the added tests kill them except the equivalent ones in equivalence_proofs. One production defect found and fixed (pending key and duplicate busy flag leaked when the queue submission raised an unexpected exception).
