second_pass.fixture_review: Real objects: the real DeferredPersistenceManager (and its real QTimer / QTest event loop in the timer tests), real QueuedMutationResult / MutationOutcomeStatus / PageSettingsPayload DTOs, a real weakref/gc check. Fakes: FakeProjectWriteService / FakeSqlWorkspaceService (tests/presentation/managers/deferred_persistence_support.py), the chaos DeferredChaosWriteService, _ScriptedLayerService, _PageViewWriteService/_SqlWorkspaceService and the per-test queue overrides. No SQL Server is involved (none available); the SQL path is the manager's queue_page_setting_if_sql boundary, so nothing here proves server behaviour. Ways the fakes were looser than the real ProjectWriteService (second pass): (1) queue_page_setting_if_sql never returned False/raised, accepted any kind (real: ValueError for 'bid_selected_page'/'view_state', kind names validated by PageSettingsPayload, all-Layers values must be [show, [uids]] and resource uid must equal the active Bid, False for no active Bid / locked Bid / sequence < 0) -> _StrictSqlPageSettingQueue test added; the bitonal and overlay_rect request literals were not pinned at all before. (2) A refused real submission returns False AND later delivers a REJECTED completion through the dispatcher; the fakes never delivered it -> late-callback test added. (3) is_expected_deferred_write_blocked(db_path, bid_uid=None) is database dependent in the real service; the fake returned a global flag so `key[1]` -> `key[0]` survived -> per-database fake test added. (4) Completion callbacks are delivered by the test synchronously and in any order; the real ones are dispatched to the main thread (single thread semantics are the same), never UNKNOWN/PROJECTION_FAILED-then-terminal in the chaos harness. (5) Writes only returned bool or raised for layer/overlay; raising for every kind and for page view / selected page (workspace) is now covered. (6) The chaos harness 'reject' queue mode is never selected. (7) Layer uid / Bid uid / page uid are shared across two databases only in the new isolation tests (real: two open files can both hold layer uid '1'). Module runtime is ~7 s on an idle machine (6 s is the bounded D10 convergence property).

second_pass.fixture_review: Fresh second-pass view of the fixtures. Real objects: AnnotationView, Page, PageViewDto, BidAnnotation, RemoteProjectionBarrier, MutationOutcomeStatus/QueuedMutationResult, EventBus, MemoryAnnotationViewRepository, UIAccessManager (db-switch test and the world), RemotePlanUpdatePipeline with the Qt thread pool, UndoRedoService, AnnotationWriteCoordinator, and a real AnnotationViewWindow in DetachedWorld (only its plan view is the module's FakeToolbarPlanView). Fakes: _WorldProjectData (a minimal Bid/Page model), the capability service (surface_access_support._Capabilities: only database_editable and page locks), licence, transaction monitor, colour service, write services, FakePlanSurfaceAccessManager (a constant), FakeConstructedWindow and a recording callback bridge. Where the fakes are looser than production: (1) _handler_manager.get_page returns a Page for EVERY uid, including the blank uid, so blank-target behaviour was unobservable there (new DetachedSecondPassWiringTests use fakes that return None for a blank uid and an end-to-end world); (2) _Capabilities does not model the SQL Server permission matrix, leases or rowversion checks, so the 'SQL permission matrix' seen by the detached surface is the UIAccessManager's Feature matrix over a two-flag capability fake, not server truth (no live SQL Server was available); (3) QtVoidCallback.request() is a same-thread direct call, so 'immediate' versus 'signalled' refresh is indistinguishable from the GUI thread; (4) the world's Config values differ from Config() defaults except snap_to_right_angle_enabled, but several same-valued booleans could not tell swapped option wirings apart (supplemental wiring-swap sweep found 7 surviving swaps, now killed by test_each_boolean_window_option_follows_only_its_own_preference); (5) the partial managers built with __new__ hide attribute renames, mitigated by real DTOs, Mock(spec=DetachedPageViewWindow) in RefreshScopeTests and the world tests. Qt wrapper validity: the manager never calls shiboken isValid (destroyed windows are matched by id); the only validity-sensitive paths use a real window deleted with shiboken delete. Every one of the 176 existing tests was read against the production code, its note written before the first-pass note was consulted; the first-pass notes were then compared and no disagreement was found. Mutation: 1195 AST mutants of detached_page_view_manager.py run in memory with fastmut2 (modal QMessageBox helpers stubbed to raise); the in-memory patcher cannot apply decorator-argument mutants (dataclass frozen), these two were run with mutrun.py and are killed.

Limitations: the support fakes are Python doubles (not the real TakeoffPlanView), the duplicate-completion guards (_sql_completion_was_applied) are shadowed by the forward-mutation token and selection revisions in the fakes, history.suspend() is not observable through FakeUndoService, geometry tests assume the offscreen platform (800x800 screen, frames present) and a clamp that equals Qt's own result is undetectable. The fixture mixes in FakeWriteService imported from another test module (tests.presentation.handlers.test_plan_view_action_handler) which is a cross-test dependency. The FakeDetachedPageData annotation_layer_hidden argument is no longer used by any test.

REAL in these tests: DetachedPageViewWindow instances (QMainWindow, real combos, buttons, timers, layouts) in the toolbar, restore, recording-plan-view and cleanup classes; the real AnnotationWriteCoordinator, AnnotationHistoryBinding and UndoRedoService behind FakeUndoService.history; real PlanSurfaceAccessState, EventBus, SelectionClipboardService, Page/Bid/BidAnnotation entities. Where the fakes are looser than the real objects: (1) FakeQueuedProjectWriteService and FakeAnnotationWriteService accept any keyword argument and always report uses_sql_collaboration_mutations True (so dropped or renamed queue kwargs went unnoticed until the exact-kwargs assertions of DetachedWindowSqlQueueTests); (2) FakeDetachedPlanView.begin_deferred_selection only bumps a revision and set_pending_mutation_uids does not drop pending items from the selection as the real plan view does, so selection restoration after completion was invisible until tests deselect explicitly; restore_annotation_styles keeps only the last call; (3) FakeUndoService.is_forward_mutation_current is true while the token is listed and bind_latest_history_to_forward_mutation is a no-op; (4) shiboken6.isValid(None) and isValid(stub) are True, so every destroyed-owner branch needs a REAL Qt object (added: deleted QDialog, deleted plan view, collected window); (5) FakeAnnotationProjectData.get_current_bid_ref is constant ('bid.mdb','7') so numeric Bid references need it patched; (6) no fake models SQL Server: the SQL queue is a recording fake, so nothing here proves server behaviour (lock refusal is a raised ActiveBidLockedError / a REJECTED result delivered by the test). Production code acting as its own oracle: expectations are literals, except page-scale conversions which use the shared domain rescale function (tested elsewhere).

second_pass.fixture_review: Read sql_server/python/ostv_sql_admin/common.py in full and environment_support. REAL: the module's validators, redaction, the atomic writer on a temp tree, argparse CLI. FAKE: pyodbc.connect/drivers (MagicMock), connections/cursors (MagicMock; looser than pyodbc: no rowcount/nextset/error classes, execute never validates SQL, so SQL text of the marker/session queries is only pinned as text), the private-file permission checks where noted (bypassed or driven by scripted os.stat_result). No real server, driver, network or /home/SQLServer is touched; passwords are only synthetic and are asserted out of reprs, errors, CLI output and JSON. Atomic private writes: the real os.replace is wrapped by environment_support.windows_safe_replace in setUp; its retry cannot mask a failure (it retries only a PermissionError on Windows, at most 40 times, then re-raises the last error; the tests that inject a failure patch os.replace with OSError, not PermissionError, and replace the wrapper for their duration); the retry helper itself is now tested (WindowsSafeReplaceHelperTests). POSIX gate: SqlAdminCommonTests (3 tests) is gated by RUNS_AS_POSIX_ROOT (os.name == posix AND geteuid() == 0). Evidence for the refinement (previously only os.name == posix): require_private_file/directory and _require_private_root raise 'must be owned by root' whenever st_uid != 0, and the tests create their files as the current user, so on a non-root Linux account the three tests ERROR instead of skipping; proven on any platform by SqlAdminPrivatePathCheckTests.test_a_file_must_be_regular_and_owned_by_root and the directory/root twins (scripted uid 1/1000 -> RuntimeError). The refined gate is applied (environment_support.RUNS_AS_POSIX_ROOT, POSIX_ROOT_REASON). New in this pass: scripted-stat tests that run the real 0600/0700/root-owner/symlink/under-root rules on every platform, atomic-write mode/ordering/descriptor-ownership tests, validator boundary cases, and the helper tests listed under added tests. Mutation: automatic sweep of common.py (348 mutants) before these tests: 255 killed, 84 survived, 9 no-verdict (import-time failures); after the new tests (final run): 326 killed, 13 survived, 9 no-verdict. The 13 survivors are PROVEN equivalent or format-only (single-operand marker guards and the symmetric compare_digest swap, the dead 'not allowed_sources' operand, the dead mkdir(...) arguments, JSON indent/sort_keys, repr=True with an explicit __repr__); of the 9 no-verdict mutants five regex-argument swaps, the set + set mutant and the __main__ guard fail at import time (killed in effect) and the two 'descriptor = -1 -> 1/2' mutants close fd 1/2 in unrelated tests so the runner cannot print a verdict: the dedicated test was run alone and KILLS them.

tests/tools/test_manage_sql_development..fixture_review: Read tools/manage_sql_development.py in full (Windows-only provisioning tool: winreg, pyodbc, WindowsCredentialStore). Every test uses pure functions, temp files, or a scripted FakeConnection/FakeCursor that records statements; winreg, the credential store, pyodbc.connect, SqlSchemaInspector/Creator are patched at the module boundary, so no SQL Server, registry key or credential is touched (the real registry/winreg helpers _registry_value/_write_registry_ownership/_remove_user_environment are intentionally never called). second_pass.fixture_review: Read tools/manage_sql_development.py in full (Windows-only provisioning tool: winreg, pyodbc, WindowsCredentialStore). REAL: the pure helpers, the atomic secrets writer on temp files, the guard/orchestration logic. FAKE: FakeConnection/FakeCursor (scripted by SQL substring; no rowcount/nextset/error classes, no T-SQL validation, so the SQL text is only pinned as recorded strings and is UNVERIFIED against a server), SqlConnectionManager and SqlSchemaInspector/Creator (stubs), WindowsCredentialStore (MagicMock), pyodbc.connect (patched), and, new in this pass, an in-memory FakeRegistry that replaces the winreg module for the registry helpers. Nothing touches the real registry, docker, network or SQL: every test class installs forbid_real_registry in setUp, which makes the real winreg.OpenKey/CreateKeyEx/SetValueEx/DeleteValue/QueryValueEx raise AssertionError, and SqlDevelopmentSetupTests proves the guard fires. A forgotten patch would otherwise have deleted real user environment variables (_remove_user_environment) or written the machine key. Secrets: passwords are synthetic, asserted out of reprs, errors and SQL text (always a bound parameter). Atomic private writes: os.replace is wrapped by the shared environment_support.windows_safe_replace (this module's second copy was removed); that retry cannot mask a failure (WindowsSafeReplaceHelperTests in test_common: only a PermissionError on Windows, at most 40 times, last error re-raised); the failure-injection tests patch os.replace/fsync with OSError. Mutation: automatic sweep of the tool (478 mutants): first run 360 killed, 115 survived, 3 no-verdict; after the first round of new tests 436/39/3; final run 462 killed, 14 survived, 2 no-verdict. One of the 14 (the cursor.close() of _drop_verified_owned_database) was then killed by an added assertion and re-checked with a named mutant; the other 13 are equivalent or format-only (equivalence_proofs): JSON indent/sort_keys, symmetric compare_digest swaps, an explicit-__repr__ dataclass flag, the blank-registry-marker operand that the UUID validation makes redundant, 'or ""' on a value only used for truthiness, and the 'descriptor = -1 -> 2' mutant that the automatic runner scores as a survivor although the dedicated descriptor test kills it when run alone (verified); the 2 no-verdict mutants are the __main__ guard.

Every call of cli.main replaces cli.FileAssociationRegistrar with a mock at the import boundary (and the default helpers are patched or checked with patched Path.exists), so the Windows registry is never touched, as the tests/README states. second_pass.fixture_review: Second pass. Real: SqlCollaborationCoordinator (_poll_once/_run_worker/_on_remote_batch/_project_session_start/resume_controlled_recovery state machine), RemoteChangeReconciliationService, ConflictResolutionService, LocalDraftRegistry + DatabaseConcurrencyTokenService, ProjectDataService, OstAggregate, LoadBidUseCase.apply_prepared and the MDB BidDataReader over a sqlite BidPages table (the page/folder rows come from the MDB reader, NOT from the SQL remote reader, so SqlRemoteChangeReader hydration SQL is not crossed). Fake: ICollaborationStore, IRemoteChangeReader, descriptor/session registries and DatabaseCapabilityService are create_autospec mocks of their interfaces (signature-checked, but they accept any return value: collaboration_status(...).state is a MagicMock so the CONFLICTED comparison is always False), and _DelayedReconciliationDispatcher is a single-thread stand-in that only defers _on_remote_batch (the real dispatcher posts every callback to the Qt thread, so interleavings between session-start and batch callbacks are limited to the ones the test builds by hand). The SQL leg is therefore fake-only: nothing here proves Change Tracking, rowversion, XACT_ABORT or applock behaviour; it proves the client-side handoff rules (navigation owner identity, ready_event, recovery/retry limits). Fake looser than production: the store never returns a connection-class error, a reset epoch or minimum_valid_version above the checkpoint, so the _poll_once epoch/retention branches are not driven by this module (covered by test_sql_collaboration_coordinator). No sleeps, polling loops or wall-clock use: every ordering is explicit (queued callback tuples), seeds not applicable. Mutation targets (the lower-layer code the assertions depend on): SqlCollaborationCoordinator (_on_remote_batch/_project_session_start/_run_worker/resume_controlled_recovery), RemoteChangeReconciliationService.apply, ProjectDataService (replace_database_hierarchy/replace_remote_bid_families/get_bid) and LoadBidUseCase._apply_prepared; AST-mutated in memory (sp4t5/*.res.jsonl) and re-run against their unit modules; the 18 integration-level survivors found in ProjectDataService.replace_database_hierarchy are closed by RemoteBatchActiveBidProjectionTests, every other final survivor is a unit-level gap listed in the findings.

second_pass.fixture_review: Second pass. Real: ConditionsSidebar (context menu, tree revision), TakeoffPlanView (selection/tool revision, context-menu owner), OstAggregate + ProjectDataService, UIEventCoordinator (object.__new__ with explicit fields: prepare_condition_duplicate_reassignment/_prepare_condition_takeoff_target), ConditionActionHandler.on_duplicate_requested/_submit_sql_condition_operation, PlanViewActionHandler.can_reassign_takeoffs/prepare_sql_property_completion/record_local_condition_reassignment, UndoRedoService, and now a real EventBus plus spec'd doubles (Mock(spec=ProjectWriteService/AnnotationWriteService/PageSettingsBar/DeferredPersistenceManager/SidebarCoordinator/ProjectReadService/PlacementCoordinator/UIAccessManager) instead of bare Mock()s; the workspace model is the real make_workspace_state_model(). Fake: the write service is a spec'd Mock, so BOTH legs stop at the service boundary: the MDB leg returns a canned WriteReloadResult and the 'SQL' leg is a queue stub whose callback the test completes by hand with a real QueuedMutationResult. Nothing here proves server behaviour (BID_LOCKED rejection is injected as a result field; T-SQL for it is UNVERIFIED and sqlite-evaluated elsewhere). Looser than production: the spec'd service never raises ActiveBidLockedError, never reorders callbacks and cannot fail after a real commit; access is a Mock(spec=UIAccessManager) with return_value booleans so per-feature denial is simulated. Qt exceptions in slots are caught by the shared selection fixture's excepthook and asserted empty at cleanup, so a raising guard cannot pass silently. second_pass.fixture_review: Read ProjectWriteService/_execute_database_mutation, DatabaseConcurrencyTokenService (per-database mutation_scope RLock in a WeakValueDictionary), _dispatch_mutation_result and the explicit executors/dispatchers in tests/helpers/sql/collaboration.py. REAL: write service, token service, draft registry, coordinator dispatch, real threads. FAKE: the mutation executors (synchronous, scripted COMMITTED/CONFLICT; they model optimistic token comparison but not rowversion, uncertain commit, deadlock victims or applock timeouts) and the capability/session fakes. Timing review: negative waits are bounded windows (_NEGATIVE_WINDOW = 0.25 s, was 0.05 s/0.2 s): a correct implementation always waits the whole window and can never fail because of it (no false failure possible: it only asserts that something has NOT happened), while a regression is detected at once. A FALSE PASS needs the second thread to be starved for longer than the window after the barrier/start; the window was widened (5x) to make that implausible. Final-state assertions do not remove the risk: in test 4 a late clear that runs after the mutation committed leaves the same final state as a correct run, and in test 5 a reload that starts after the commit also reads the committed value (I tried a 'held reader' design that took its snapshot on entry and answered after the mutation finished; it only detects a reload that enters inside the window, which the window check already detects, so it was reverted instead of kept as a misleading 'deterministic' claim). Residual risk (documented, not removable without production hooks): a negative-only check is inherently probabilistic. The positive waits (wait(1)/join(2)) fail only if a thread is starved for seconds.

second_pass.fixture_review: Second pass. Real: DetachedPageViewManager, AnnotationViewWindow, MeshViewWindow, OpenGLViewer (renderer replaced by MeshRendererBoundary/FakeMeshScene: no GL), TakeoffPlanView x2 (main + detached), PageSettingsBar, ViewerSyncCoordinator, UIEventCoordinator (object.__new__ with only the fields each handler reads), DeferredPersistenceManager, UndoRedoService, EventBus, PlanViewActionHandler (paste/insert completions), MenuController/MainWindow methods bound onto small owners, real PDFRenderingService + PageCache + NativePageImagePlaneProvider + CompositeRenderer over solid-colour TIFF/PDF files in temp dirs, real RemoteChangeReconciliationService (texture-only/overlay tests). Doubles: SharedPageData(FakeProjectData), FakeProjectWriteService/FakeSqlWorkspaceService queues whose callbacks are completed by hand with real QueuedMutationResult values (the SQL leg is a fake queue: no server, no lease, no ordering guarantee beyond the order the test calls the callbacks), a manual thread pool/bridge for the remote plan pipeline, spec'd Mocks (SidebarCoordinator, PageComboBox, DeferredPersistenceManager, QtVoidCallback, OpenGLViewer). Timing: one event-driven _wait_until (blocks on the next Qt event; the QTimer only bounds a FAILING run at 10 s); _wait_for_scene_colors asserts after the wait, _wait_for_pages_loaded now asserts the wait succeeded (second-pass hardening, previously a timed-out wait was silently ignored). Load check: the module minus the 50 s matrix test was run 18x in 3 parallel streams on a machine already loaded with 6-9 mutation workers (73 tests each, OK every time), and the two same-path replacement tests 48x in 4 streams (OK); the one earlier combined-run failure of test_same_size_and_timestamp_replacement_repaints_both_plan_surfaces could not be reproduced (see findings). Independence: pixel tests compare scene centre pixels of a 64x64 render of the scene rect (widgets resized to 300x300, offscreen), no fonts, DPI or screen geometry; deterministic file contents; no seeds. Fakes looser than production: FakeRenderingService answers requests only when the test calls the stored callback, PDF rasterisation is real but single-worker, ProjectData is one shared in-memory object (no hydration lag), and GL/mesh generation is faked (only texture/scene identity and enablement are real). Second-pass hardening in this round: _wait_for_renders_idle (no tracked render request in flight before the same-path tests rewrite the TIFF in place; the one earlier combined-run failure is still unreproduced, a torn read of an in-flight render is the hypothesis), plus SceneNavigationControlsZoomDisplayTests for the control that has no unit module. Mutation targets: DetachedPageViewManager, ViewerSyncCoordinator, UIEventCoordinator, RemotePlanUpdatePipeline, DeferredPersistenceManager, MeshViewWindow, MenuController, SceneNavigationControls and PlanViewActionHandler; sweeps use per-line covering tests (the 50 s four-surface matrix test excluded from the sweep and evaluated separately on a sample).

tests/presentation/services/test_annotat.fixture_review: New module (the coordinator had no mirrored primary test, only indirect coverage from the handler/window suites). Real collaborators: ProjectDataService over a real OstAggregate (the projection the coordinator updates: positions, text, styles, named-view rename, add/remove annotations, layer visibility synchronisation, annotation-layer lookup), the real EventBus (it builds AnnotationsChangedEvent from the published payload, so a wrong key fails loudly), real BidAnnotation/Page/InsertAnnotationSpec/PasteRefRemap/DTOs and the real UndoRedoService in one end-to-end Hot Link history test. Explicit fakes: _WriteService (the AnnotationWriteService surface with the real parameter names and defaults, recording every call and returning configured results) and _Undo (records suspend/rebind). Drift guards: signature-equality tests against the real AnnotationWriteService and UndoRedoService. No SQL Server or Access database is involved: the coordinator is a synchronous projection/event component; queued-vs-local routing is expressed through the injected execute_paste callable and the project_* completion entry points, and there is no queue, thread, generation token or Qt owner inside this class (those live in the SQL coordinator and the handlers), so cancellation, stale generation, ordering and destroyed-owner cases are covered by the tests of those callers; what exists here (failed write, duplicate completion, partial identity map, empty batches, missing/foreign annotations, unavailable restore outcomes) is tested directly. Mutation result with only this module: 199 killed of 225 AST mutants (11 more killed by the in-process runner for structurally unsupported ones); 15 survivors are all proven equivalent (see equivalence_proofs).

second_pass.fixture_review: STATIC REVIEW ONLY: all four tests are live-gated and skipped here (no SQL Server); I did not run them. Independent read of SqlProjectWriter._validate_mutation_locks (writer.py ~L624-790). The bid_locked branch is 'UNION ALL SELECT -1, N'bid_locked', NULL, NULL, NULL FROM @MutationResources r JOIN [dbo].[Bids] b ON b.UID=r.BidUID JOIN [dbo].[JobStatuses] s ON s.UID=b.JobStatusUID WHERE ?=0 AND r.ResourceType<>N'bid' AND r.BidUID IS NOT NULL AND (s.Locked IS NULL OR s.Locked=1)'. Parameter order checked against the 14 placeholders (payload x3, session, session, child-block flag, session, editor-block flag, session, stale seconds, session x3, bid_lock_exempt last): consistent. Semantics: inner JOIN on JobStatuses makes a NULL or dangling JobStatusUID an unlocked Bid; NULL Locked is treated as locked (fail-safe); Priority -1 sorts first under ORDER BY [Priority] with TOP (1), so a locked Bid wins over every lease/rowversion violation; column count/types of the UNION branch match the other branches (int, nvarchar, nvarchar/NULL, int/NULL, varbinary/NULL); the preceding statement ends with ';' so WITH is legal. The 'r.BidUID IS NOT NULL' predicate is redundant on a server (the inner join already excludes NULL). The operation's before_commit hooks use writer._connection(), which yields the ACTIVE mutation's lease (same transaction), so the status-flip tests update the Bid inside the write transaction as intended. Would the tests fail on a regression against a real server? Yes for: deleting the branch, dropping 'Locked IS NULL' (NULL case), dropping '=1' (locked case), making the join LEFT (NULL-status Bid refused), dropping the resource-type exemption (status change/delete/move shapes refused), inverting ?=0 (exempt case), mis-ordering parameters (type error), removing the Exclusive/Shared 'OSTV:bid:<uid>' acquisition (race test: B's status change would not time out). NOT covered by any scenario: the Priority -1 ordering against a coexisting lease conflict (a regression to a low priority would pass all four tests) and the predicate 'BidUID IS NOT NULL' (equivalent on a server). Change: the dangling-status test caught every Exception and skipped; that could hide a permission or syntax error as a skip, it now skips only on pyodbc.IntegrityError (a foreign key forbidding the dangling row; the reference schema has no such key). Decision B1 not reopened.

tests/tools/test_audit_sql_integration_e.fixture_review: NEW module (the first pass recorded that tools/audit_sql_integration_environment.py had no tests). Feasibility decision: yes, a deterministic fake-based module is possible because main() is a thin wrapper: one pyodbc.connect, one SELECT, a directory listing and a table of expected values. Everything external is replaced: pyodbc.connect is patched in every test (returns a scripted connection whose cursor records the SQL and returns a tuple), ProgramData is a temporary directory, stdout is captured. No server, registry, docker or network is touched. REAL: main()'s result mapping, exit-code table and JSON output. FAKE: the connection/cursor. Fakes looser than SQL Server: the SELECT is never executed, so the T-SQL (counts of databases, logins, sessions, cursors, markers, signed procedures, grants, client database state) is UNVERIFIED; only the positional contract between the SELECT list and the row indexes is pinned (fragments of the SQL text must appear in the order of the result keys). Independence: HEALTHY_COUNTS and SELECT_ORDER are literals written from the tool's documented expectations, not read from the tool. Mutation: automatic sweep of the tool (99 mutants): 97 killed, 2 not killed (the __main__ guard, unobservable in-process). Finding: a missing backup directory makes main() raise FileNotFoundError (traceback, non-zero exit) instead of reporting 'backup_files: 0' or failing cleanly; the test only pins that it is never a healthy audit (any OSError), not the exact failure.

skip_audit.cursor_3: Need QT_QPA_PLATFORM=windows; legitimate. Both cursor modules ran 9/9 OK under the windows platform on an unlocked desktop (a locked desktop makes GetCursorPos fail). Reinstating the original winId() defect fails 12 native subtests.

decisions.decision: Enforce the Bid lock inside the SQL writer transaction (analysis 2026-10-02: business rule, deliberate since fc7f470 2026-03-29; SQL backend 2026-07-18 never mirrored the Access guard)
decisions.status: fixed (option B, server-side writer check; T-SQL UNVERIFIED against a live server)
decisions.outcome: No code change. The Bid lock is an in-memory client flag (is_current_bid_locked, set on Bid selection, database refresh and snapshot restore) consumed by the UI _LOCK_BLOCKED set and by ActiveBidWriteGuard (legacy synchronous commands, active Bid only). Probe (SCRATCH d14_probe.py): with the active Bid locked all 69 SQL queue_* entries were accepted at submission and the queued work executed in 68 (placement has no use-case call in the harness). Nothing is checked in the coordinator, the writer, a trigger or SQL permissions (clients hold db_datawriter on dbo). 28 entry-point rows are in SCRATCH\fragments\dec2-d12-lockedbid.json findings. Ranked exposure: (1) no server-side or worker-time check; (2) condition folder create/rename/delete/move succeed on a locked Bid over SQL (EDIT_CONDITION_STRUCTURE not lock-blocked, SQL queue paths carry no guard; Access paths blocked at the service); (3) stale windows: writes queued before the lock, dialogs freezing lock state at open (Cover Sheet, Edit Condition), undo/redo closures, detached-window access copies; (4) page-setting sites with no inner gate relying on widget enabled state; (5) non-UI actors: other clients, older builds, scripts, any db_datawriter login. Not exposures: MCP (read-only by contract), export, tools/sql_server provisioning, workspace-state writes, import (cannot target an existing Bid), and Bid delete/duplicate/move/status/master-data writes allowed by design.

decisions.decision: classify_pyodbc_error: number/SQLSTATE first, anchored text fallback
decisions.outcome: Rule order: SQLSTATE 23; 28000/18456; 4060; 229/262/297; HYT00/HYT01; anchored text (certificate, database, permission, timeout; re.match at the start of each diagnostic record after stripping the [state][Microsoft][ODBC Driver ..][SQL Server] prefix; only for records reporting no non-zero native number); SQLSTATE 08 or connection numbers 53/64/233/10054/10060; UNKNOWN. Reproduced (about 150 failing subtests): a 3960 message echoing a database named Permissions_Test classified as PERMISSION_DENIED. 11 tests x 13 echoed names covering 1205/1222/3960, constraints 547/2627/2601, permission/login/database/connection; all mutants killed. native_code semantics, user messages and recovery flags unchanged; no existing test edited. decisions.decision: Refresh on an ended worker is the explicit re-probe with bounded backoff
decisions.outcome: There is no user-facing Refresh command; the only route into the coordinator is the DATABASE_REFRESHED event. _on_database_refreshed now checks _worker_has_ended first; if conflicts were cleared it republishes capabilities (handler restarts), otherwise it calls the new _restart_ended_worker (shared with the capabilities handler): the unchanged D13 _admit_reprobe_restart backoff, then stop reconfigured and start after a clean stop. A refresh inside the backoff window is dropped, not queued; a live worker, unstarted thread or unknown database is untouched and spends no backoff. Per failure kind: session_expired reconnects; credential_required only if credentials exist; read-only/trust change and non-retryable errors end again if the cause persists; failed first open restarts as a normal start. 10 tests (12 failures before), D9 pins and D13 RestartRule tests stay green under both dispatchers; one D13 pin changed contract (noted); 10 of 10 mutants killed. FINDING (decision): DATABASE_REFRESHED is also published after routine post-write reloads, compaction, the Access change monitor and external reconciliation, so it is not strictly a user gesture: a worker that ends right after a write restarts once immediately without a user click (bounded by the backoff). A strictly user-initiated trigger would need a dedicated event or command.
decisions.note: Superseded in part by G1: DATABASE_REFRESHED now restarts an ended worker only for recoverable end reasons.

decisions.decision: Marker-query-blocked behaviour pinned
decisions.outcome: No production change. With the old writer holding the operation applock, query_operation gets sp_getapplock -1 and raises SqlInfrastructureError LOCKED ("Another session is resolving the same SQL operation."), non-retryable; the worker ends; the operation stays UNCERTAIN (journal record and _uncertain_callbacks entry kept); zero DML replayed; the marker SELECT never runs even if the marker is committed; the failed lookup is rolled back and its connection closed. Once the old writer connection is gone a Refresh restarts the worker and recovery resolves the operation from the marker (COMMITTED/FAILED_BEFORE_COMMIT) with no replay. 2 tests x marker-absent/marker-committed (direct + real worker under the UI dispatcher), 9 of 9 mutants killed. GAP (not changed): the user-visible message is exactly the LOCKED text in the disconnected state; it does NOT tell the user to reconnect. The strict SQL model answers applock -1 immediately (the real 10 s @LockTimeout stall is not modelled).
decisions.note: G2 added reconnect guidance to the user message; F6 pins updated by decision.

decisions.decision: DATABASE_REFRESHED restarts an ended worker only for recoverable end reasons
decisions.outcome: Worker end reason recorded as a private enum _WorkerEndReason on _DatabaseRuntime.end_reason. Recoverable (refresh restarts through the unchanged bounded backoff, injectable clock): LOCKED-uncertain (marker lookup blocked by the old writer lock) and a transient failed first open without retry (DatabaseCatalogError/OSError). Not recoverable (stay stopped until credential re-entry or Reconnect): stop requested, session_expired, credential_required, read_only_required (incl. trust change after connecting), non-retryable error without a flag, unexpected internal error. Suspension gap and ValueError do not end the worker; a retryable failure after establishment never ends it. Clearing conflicts for an unrecoverable end republishes DATABASE_CAPABILITIES_CHANGED inside the own-event guard so nothing restarts. The D13 capability handler is unchanged (it still restarts any ended worker; the coordinator is the only production publisher; no test showed it reintroducing the loop). 17 failures before; 13 new/changed tests; D9 pins (both dispatchers) and the 10 D13 RestartRule tests (UI dispatcher; sync variants in the Refresh tests) green; 18 mutants killed. Caveat: blocked-marker is detected by phase, not exception type, so a flagless error such as database-missing in that phase would classify the same (practically unreachable; a precise check needs a new field on DatabaseCatalogError). AGENTS.md F3 sentence replaced by one restricted sentence.

decisions.decision: Writer-side lock rule in _validate_mutation_locks
decisions.status: fixed (T-SQL unverified against a live server)
decisions.outcome: New UNION ALL branch (Priority -1, kind bid_locked) in SqlProjectWriter._validate_mutation_locks inside the existing validation batch, after the operation-marker check and the sorted applocks, before the operation. Inner-joins Bids to JobStatuses; applies only to resources with type <> bid and a bid_uid; a Bid counts as locked when Locked IS NULL OR Locked = 1. JobStatuses.Locked is a NULLABLE bit (YESNO, required=False, no default); the client serialises NULL as the string NULL so NULL means locked; a dangling or NULL JobStatusUID or a missing Bids row means unlocked (matches settings_reader._parse_job_statuses). No UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK on Bids or JobStatuses: the race is serialised by the Shared child applock against the Exclusive status-writer applock (inference; accepted: a Job Status Locked flag edited concurrently by master data is an accepted race). Refusal is raised before the operation and rolled back: nothing written, no lease consumed; a committed retry is recovered before the check runs. Exemption: DatabaseMutationRequest.bid_lock_exempt (not in the request hash, not forgeable via payload) set only by ProjectWriteService.queue_cancelled_placement_cleanup_delete (takeoffs only; also skips the client queue-time guard); an AST scan test confirms nothing else sets it. Resource shape: bid/project_bids/projects_collection (status change, delete, duplicate, move), master data and import are exempt. Over the 69 real queue_* commands 22 are allowed on a locked Bid and 47 refused; every writer refusal is already a client queue-time refusal except queue_takeoff_placement (rejected when its work runs); Bid moves are refused by the client but allowed by the writer. SQL_SCHEMA_V1 and its checksum untouched; no triggers. PROCESS NOTE: the stage-1 agent wrote production before tests, so failing-first is not literal; the failing-before proof is the in-memory rule-removed mutant. decisions.decision: One operation id never reports two different terminal statuses
decisions.outcome: SqlCollaborationOperationTerminalStatusContractTests (7 tests; main test runs 1,296 deterministic event orders against the real coordinator: commit, unknown-then-committed/lost, failed, rejected, BID_LOCKED, conflict, cancel, double cancel, stop, trust loss, duplicate submission, projection failure, late cancel, raising callback, immediate/delayed dispatch) asserts at most one distinct terminal status, exactly one closing terminal, nothing after it, interim statuses only before it, the write never replayed, no leaked journal/callback entries; 18 delivery sequences pinned; terminal = COMMITTED, REJECTED, CONFLICT, FAILED_BEFORE_COMMIT, CANCELLED_BEFORE_START; interim = COMMIT_STATUS_UNKNOWN, COMMITTED_PROJECTION_FAILED. 9 coordinator mutants killed; survivors (M9, M13, E1-E3) are outside the one-terminal contract. The contract holds per submission; two repeats exist, both only reachable by reusing an operation id (production uses uuid4): a COMMITTED whose callback raised is re-delivered as COMMITTED, and a duplicate submission of a live id gets its own REJECTED on its own callback while the original later reports COMMITTED. Consequence: for window.py mutant #1230 the status test in _sql_completion_was_applied is redundant for generated ids. Reusing an id after its terminal status is accepted as a new submission; only the server-side marker protects that case. AGENTS.md sentence added.

decisions.decision: Audit what a generic exception from the Plan reassignment submit helper leaves behind at every layer; reuse the R4 unwind if anything remains; keep ActiveBidLockedError silent refusal and the F4 once-guards.
decisions.outcome: DEFECT CONFIRMED AND FIXED at two places. (1) condition_action_handler.on_duplicate_requested: _submit_sql_condition_operation re-raises any exception other than ActiveBidLockedError/RuntimeError/ValueError (KeyError, OSError, AttributeError, ...) after freeing only the pending key, and abort() sat after the call (run only for a falsy return), so the prepared Plan completion leaked at a generic error: pending marks on the Plan (the selected Takeoffs stayed dimmed), the held forward-mutation token (undo/redo blocked, can_undo False), the cleared selection; RuntimeError/ValueError/ActiveBidLockedError were already clean (abort via the falsy return). Fix: the call is wrapped, abort() runs (its own failure is logged, never replacing the queue error) and the SAME exception is re-raised; and the helper's terminal once-guard is now set whenever submit raises (all three except branches), so a callback the queue retained before raising can no longer place the copies (probe: with an empty prior Plan selection a late COMMITTED callback DID reach _finish_condition_duplicate in the real stack; only the selection-revision bump of a non-empty restore stopped it). (2) plan_view_action_handler.prepare_sql_property_completion (shared with _queue_sql_plan_properties, which calls it OUTSIDE its try): an exception after begin_forward_mutation (page identities, selection identities, pending marks) leaked the forward-mutation token and the handler pending marks; now _unwind_failed_preparation (marks released, token finished, each step isolated and logged) runs and the same exception is re-raised. Layer audit: _pending_sql_operations key freed at every exit; pending Plan marks: fixed; deferred selection: restored by abort (restore_failed_selection) and begin_deferred_selection is a bare integer increment that cannot raise; forward-mutation token: fixed; edit lease: the reassignment path never requests or holds a ModalEditLeaseSession/plan edit lease (prepare only RELEASES the geometry lease before beginning; asserted: no lease call on the write service, handler lease handle None); optimistic placement/duplicated condition state: placement only happens inside committed(), which cannot run for a failed submit (once-guard) and no condition state exists before the commit; the prepared completion: abort sets its terminal flag so it can never apply history afterwards, and nothing ever queues a second reassignment (queue_conditions_duplicate called once, queue_plan_properties never). project_write_service.queue_conditions_duplicate registers nothing before queue_request (read-only resource/ownership capture), so a raise there needs no cleanup; a raise inside queue_request after _pending_mutations.begin is a coordinator-layer question (finding).

decisions.decision: BidPlanrooms spelling follow-up: report only (collation, DDL, checksum, smallest stable fix).
decisions.outcome: REPORT ONLY, no change made. VERIFIED BY RUNNING CODE (read-only probes SCRATCH\dec10_s4_probe.py and dec10_s4_spell.py, in-memory dataclasses.replace of the model, no file edits) vs INFERRED is marked. (a) COLLATION: infrastructure/sql/database_creator.py:create_database executes exactly `CREATE DATABASE [<name>]` (line 208) with no COLLATE clause, so a new database inherits the server default (the model database collation); no code in ost_visualizer (grep 'collat' over the whole tree, tools and sql_server) sets or reads a collation; render_sql_server_schema emits no COLLATE on any column or table; tools/manage_sql_development.py:403 and tools/provision_sql_integration.py:239 also create databases without COLLATE (their COLLATE Latin1_General_100_BIN2 uses are only name-marker comparisons in provisioning scripts). Assumed case-insensitivity: (1) schema_validator._validate_core_constraints casefold fallback for foreign keys (schema_validator.py:~203-208) is the only production place that tolerates the spelling; (2) tests state it (tests/integration/sql/test_schema_contract.py:129 resolves table names through a casefold map 'as on the default server collation'; strict_sql_fakes.py:181 compares identifiers case-insensitively). VERIFIED: of 100 bracketed [dbo]/[ostv] table references in production SQL strings every one matches a model table spelling exactly, and the model has 64 tables / 83 foreign keys / 131 indexes where the ONLY spelling mismatch (table, column, index, FK parent or child) is the child table of FK BidPlanrooms_BidUID1; no two table names collide when casefolded. INFERRED (no live server): on a case-sensitive server collation CREATE TABLE [BidPlanRooms] succeeds and only ALTER TABLE [dbo].[BidPlanrooms] ... fails (Msg 4902, object not found), aborting initialization inside the schema-lock transaction. (b) A casefold resolver in render_sql_server_schema (VERIFIED by rendering the model with child_table/parent_table of every FK replaced by the spelling of the casefold map): 278 rendered statements before and after; exactly ONE differs (index 246): before `ALTER TABLE [dbo].[BidPlanrooms] ADD CONSTRAINT [BidPlanrooms_BidUID1] FOREIGN KEY ([BidUID]) REFERENCES [dbo].[Bids] ([UID])`, after `ALTER TABLE [dbo].[BidPlanRooms] ADD CONSTRAINT [BidPlanrooms_BidUID1] FOREIGN KEY ([BidUID]) REFERENCES [dbo].[Bids] ([UID])` (constraint name keeps the vendor spelling); all 64 CREATE TABLE, 131 CREATE INDEX and the other 82 FK statements are byte-identical. (c) CHECKSUM: schema_definition.py SqlSchemaDefinition.checksum is sha256 over '\n-- statement --\n'.join(self.statements) (= render_sql_server_schema(core_schema) + the ostv extension statements) followed by the canonical_database_requirements; VERIFIED: recomputing it that way reproduces the pin. It therefore hashes the RENDERED DDL TEXT, not the model, so every variant that changes that one statement changes the checksum. Pinned value 0cecca4baced14d54832a90ead0bac84e743875abca98b0eb173903491dec23c (literal pin tests/infrastructure/sql/test_schema_definition.py:158; also test_the_checksum_is_the_sha256_of_statements_then_requirements, ..._depends_on_every_part_of_the_definition, ..._is_stable_across_reads). VERIFIED values: current 0cecca4b...; resolver in the renderer 53ee835fef3347f213bb23c62ea273d9b5bb98f45ea06cfe0f29c43ee1c37287; one-token metadata edit (child_table BidPlanrooms->BidPlanRooms only, reference_schema_metadata.py:464) 53ee835f... (identical to the resolver, because the rendered text is identical; the fixture tests/fixtures/reference_mdb_schema.json:1786 and the Access acceptance test tests/integration/mdb/test_schema_acceptance.py:709 are not hashed, they only pin the vendor MDB spelling and would have to follow the metadata edit); a variant that also renames the constraint to BidPlanRooms_BidUID1 b2a0a3a9...8ed8bd77 (a different value again, not needed). Consequence (read from code): database_creator.py:538 records SQL_SCHEMA_V1.checksum in the new database and schema_validator.py:45 / client_permissions.py:169 (schema_record_is_canonical) reject any database whose stored checksum differs, so every database created with the current v1 would stop validating; AGENTS.md ('only SQL schema is checksummed version 1 ... no alternate checksums, compatibility aliases or runtime upgrade paths; a database that does not validate exactly as canonical v1 is rejected') forbids bridging that, so changing the text is a re-baseline of v1 (new literal pin, databases recreated), acceptable only if no deployed v1 database must survive (not known to me). (d) SMALLEST CHANGE THAT KEEPS THE CHECKSUM VALUE: only one that leaves SqlSchemaDefinition.statements untouched, i.e. a resolver applied at EXECUTION time (database_creator.initialize_blank_database loop `for statement in SQL_SCHEMA_V1.statements: cursor.execute(statement)` resolving the FK table identifiers through a casefold map of the model tables before execute): VERIFIED that statements and the checksum are then unchanged (checksum recomputed unchanged); INFERRED that the validator still passes (its FK casefold fallback and exact table-name checks accept the stored spelling). Cost: the hashed DDL is no longer byte-for-byte the DDL that runs, which weakens the checksum's meaning, and it duplicates a second rendering rule; a render-time resolver or any model edit changes the checksum as shown. Recommended: no change unless a case-sensitive server must be supported (UNVERIFIED that any customer runs one; the default server collation is case-insensitive); if it must, accept the v1 re-baseline with the metadata one-token edit (smallest, keeps one DDL text) rather than an execution-time rewrite.

decisions.decision: ServiceContainer follow-ups: dead branch and None-returning factories
decisions.outcome: The unreachable plain-factory branch in get() was removed after a whole-suite line trace and a static caller check showed it was never reached. No registered singleton factory can return None (12 register_singleton sites reviewed), so the private-sentinel change was not needed; the current contract (a None product is rebuilt on every get) is pinned by a test, together with falsy-product caching and factory release on clear. 21 in-memory mutants of the container are killed.

decisions.decision: Left column splitter resizing and scroll freezes on composite Plans
decisions.outcome: Layers stretch set to 0 so only the Conditions pane absorbs Pan-handle and window height changes (real-window tests for shrink, grow, Conditions or Layers hidden, Pan toggle, window resize and restart). Scroll freeze traced to PySide QImage calls holding the GIL on render workers; large conversions, effects, tints and overlay crops now run in BAND_PIXELS bands with byte-identical output (GUI stall per composite frame about 65 ms to about 25 ms). Scrolling itself, the Pan sidebar and the debounce were measured and are not causes; remaining GIL holders and the placement-mode pdfium_lock use are reported, not changed.
